article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Just Revealed 7 New Rules for Prompting Claude 5 Models

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian engineering argument: instead of investing in more eval harnesses, invest in interfaces that expose verifiable artifacts.
article_ideas.audience: AI product engineers, PMs, and eval teams
article_ideas.based_on: If a product is hard to evaluate, it is poorly designed for human verification.
article_ideas.thesis: If an AI feature is difficult to evaluate, it is not an evaluation problem—it is a product design failure: once a product exposes its assumptions, intermediate steps and provenance, users can verify it and eval becomes tractable.
article_ideas.title: 'I can't eval it' is a product smell: how to make AI explainable enough to test
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping AI Nobody Can Verify with Hamel Husain

article_ideas.angle: Process and culture for eval teams, drawing on active-learning/data-bottleneck arguments.
article_ideas.audience: ML/agent evaluation engineers and team leads
article_ideas.based_on: Looking at even 10 to 20 traces
article_ideas.thesis: Automated eval frameworks that are built before any manual trace inspection optimize for the wrong categories; a mandatory 10-20 trace review is the only way to choose metrics that actually track user-facing failures.
article_ideas.title: The 20-trace ritual: why manual inspection is the foundation of agent evaluation
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping AI Nobody Can Verify with Hamel Husain

article_ideas.angle: Design model for safe adoption in regulated/professional domains.
article_ideas.audience: Applied data scientists, AI product designers, domain experts
article_ideas.based_on: Domain experts will not sign off on black-box outputs they cannot verify.
article_ideas.thesis: For high-stakes domains, expert sign-off requires surfacing contradictions, key facts, and open questions in an implicit fact-finding workflow; black-box outputs will never be approved, no matter how good the eval metrics look.
article_ideas.title: Your AI assistant should produce an evidence dossier, not an answer
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping AI Nobody Can Verify with Hamel Husain

article_ideas.angle: Counterpoint to fear of agents: they can be used to build their own eval tooling.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform and eval infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Use coding agents to quickly render interfaces for reviewing traces
article_ideas.thesis: Coding agents excel at building trace-review UIs, and using them to reduce the tedium of manual data inspection is the fastest path to evals that people actually run; evaluators should treat agents as their first eval infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: Let agents build the test harnesses agents deserve
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping AI Nobody Can Verify with Hamel Husain

article_ideas.angle: Engineering and design-systems argument for shifting from prompt-level interventions to schema-level contract design in agentic UI.
article_ideas.audience: Frontend engineers, design-system maintainers, and AI platform teams.
article_ideas.based_on: The component catalog is the critical contract between the agent and the UI; every property and constraint matters.
article_ideas.thesis: Design systems should be treated as machine-readable constraints, not prose documentation; when the component catalog defines every valid property and constraint, schema violations—not prompt wording—become the controllable source of off-brand UI.
article_ideas.title: The Component Catalog Is the New Contract: Why Prompt Tuning Can't Fix Generated UI
article_ideas.video_title: The End of the Static Screen: Architecting Intent-Driven UX — Gus Iwanaga, commercetools

article_ideas.angle: Decision-oriented architecture piece comparing the three rendering protocols and their consequences for validation, observability, and trust.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, engineering leaders, and product engineers building agentic experiences.
article_ideas.based_on: Choosing the protocol is an architectural decision because it determines determinism, design system compliance, flexibility, and security risk in advance.
article_ideas.thesis: Selecting the UI rendering protocol is an architectural decision that must be made per surface based on determinism, brand compliance, and security risk—not as a statement about how 'smart' the AI should be.
article_ideas.title: Choose Your Agent's Leash: A Practical Guide to Controlled, Declarative, and Open-Ended UI Rendering
article_ideas.video_title: The End of the Static Screen: Architecting Intent-Driven UX — Gus Iwanaga, commercetools

article_ideas.angle: Pattern essay linking atomic design to generative UI: constraints on the layout skeleton are the interface-level analogue of type and token rules for LLM outputs.
article_ideas.audience: UX designers, design-system practitioners, and frontend engineers building AI-native interfaces.
article_ideas.based_on: Atomic design provides a practical two-level pattern for generative UI: use a top-down slot/sub-slot layout skeleton for information architecture and a bottom-up curated component catalog for content.
article_ideas.thesis: LLM-determined layout is random, but teams can make generated interfaces coherent by combining a top-down slot and sub-slot page skeleton with a bottom-up curated component catalog—deterministic structure, flexible content.
article_ideas.title: Atomic Design Is the Missing Guardrail for Generative UX
article_ideas.video_title: The End of the Static Screen: Architecting Intent-Driven UX — Gus Iwanaga, commercetools

article_ideas.angle: Practice-oriented thought piece for design leadership on how review, handoff, and hiring change when the schema is the interface.
article_ideas.audience: UX/design leaders and product executives investing in AI-driven user experiences.
article_ideas.based_on: UX teams must shift from designing individual pixels to defining systems, schemas, catalogs, and rules.
article_ideas.thesis: When an agent assembles UI from intent, the design team's primary deliverable is no longer static mockups; it is machine-readable schemas, component catalogs, and composition rules, and this shift must reshape design org processes today.
article_ideas.title: Design Leaders Will Ship Schemas, Not Screens
article_ideas.video_title: The End of the Static Screen: Architecting Intent-Driven UX — Gus Iwanaga, commercetools

article_ideas.angle: Argue that standard permission systems are insufficient for money-moving agents and propose separating the three questions at the system level.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and staff architects
article_ideas.based_on: Can we prove it later?
article_ideas.thesis: The three-question model shows that consent, runtime scope, and durable proof are separate responsibilities; most agent frameworks solve only the first and then cannot answer 'can we prove it later?' in a dispute. Building an evidence store as a first-class component is the architectural line between playful agents and financially-safe agents.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Permission Check Is Not Authorization—You Need an Evidence Pipeline
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Just Authorized What?! — Jay Mok & Ben Coumes, Paypal

article_ideas.angle: A cautionary argument that medium-stakes known-party reliance on logs is a transient phase; open verification eventually becomes needed as agent boundaries expand.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs and enterprise architects adopting agentic commerce
article_ideas.based_on: Closed ecosystems simplify dispute handling via transaction logs
article_ideas.thesis: Closed ecosystems reduce friction today, but when an agent acts against a user the platform logs cannot protect the user from the platform's own blind spots or from a compromised agent inside the trust boundary. Basing dispute resolution on platform-held logs means the platform is the final judge, which is a weak guarantee for open commerce.
article_ideas.title: Known Counterparties Are a Security Falsity: Why Closed Ecosystems Give You False Comfort
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Just Authorized What?! — Jay Mok & Ben Coumes, Paypal

article_ideas.angle: Present PayPal's approval token as a general pattern for constrained, time-boxed credentials in agent systems.
article_ideas.audience: Backend and identity engineers working on agent tool calls
article_ideas.based_on: amount, merchant, and expiry information in an opaque string
article_ideas.thesis: Long-lived OAuth scopes are the wrong abstraction for autonomous agents because they grant all-or-nothing access without fine-grained, expiring constraints. Approval tokens—opaque, merchant/amount/expiry-bound artifacts—are a concrete alternative that preserves user control while letting agents move fast.
article_ideas.title: Stop Minting Broad OAuth Scopes for Your Agents: Use Approval Tokens Instead
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Just Authorized What?! — Jay Mok & Ben Coumes, Paypal

article_ideas.angle: Generalize beyond money movement to show the architectural primitive is about irreversible actions, not just payments.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure and platform teams building regulated agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: Any domain involving irreversible agent actions can leverage signed mandates and verifiable tokens.
article_ideas.thesis: The same signed-intent plus verifiable-token pattern applies to medical orders, e-signatures, and securities trading; domains that currently invent bespoke consent mechanisms should instead reuse a general, cross-domain verifiable-intent layer.
article_ideas.title: Signed Mandates Are Not Just for Payments: Verifiable Intent Is General Agent Middleware
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Just Authorized What?! — Jay Mok & Ben Coumes, Paypal

article_ideas.angle: Business-model analysis of Wafer's pivot from GPU optimization software to running open-source LLMs internally
article_ideas.audience: AI startup founders, infrastructure investors, technical operators at YC-stage companies
article_ideas.based_on: Shifted from selling GPU optimization software to companies to running open-source LLMs internally using their own agents.
article_ideas.thesis: When an agent can reliably optimize inference, the business should capture the value by running the optimized model itself: vertical integration creates production telemetry that feeds the next optimization loop and makes the company more defensible than a standalone software tool.
article_ideas.title: Don't Sell the Optimization Tool; Operate the Optimized Inference Cloud
article_ideas.video_title: Building AI That Optimizes AI

article_ideas.angle: Model evaluation and procurement from a serving-economics point of view
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI teams, machine learning platform engineers, AI infrastructure buyers
article_ideas.based_on: Open-source models paired with Wafer's optimization match or beat proprietary models at a fraction of the cost.
article_ideas.thesis: With an agentic inference layer, open-source models no longer compete only on weights; their serving stacks can match or beat proprietary APIs at a fraction of the cost, so model procurement decisions must include the serving/optimization layer.
article_ideas.title: Open Weights Plus Optimized Serving Beat Proprietary APIs on Real-World Cost-Performance
article_ideas.video_title: Building AI That Optimizes AI

article_ideas.angle: Go-to-market and product design for inference clouds serving production agents
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure leadership, enterprise platform teams, LLM operations buyers
article_ideas.based_on: Latency improvement, quantified per inference call, drives enterprise vendor switching in production agent workloads
article_ideas.thesis: A measured 30-50% improvement in per-call latency and cost induces enterprises to switch inference vendors, so AI infrastructure startups should sell enforceable latency/cost contracts rather than competing on model catalog breadth.
article_ideas.title: Per-Call Performance Contracts Are the Real AI Infrastructure Moat
article_ideas.video_title: Building AI That Optimizes AI

article_ideas.angle: Architecture frontier for heterogeneous AI compute
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure architects, GPU platform teams, AI systems engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Agents tune every layer of the stack for whatever silicon wins on price-performance.
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic per-layer tuning will make NVIDIA, AMD, and TPU choices a dynamic scheduling decision, so application and serving code should treat silicon as replaceable infrastructure behind a model-serving layer.
article_ideas.title: From Vendor-Shaped Code to Agent-Routed Silicon: Heterogeneous GPUs Become a Scheduling Surface
article_ideas.video_title: Building AI That Optimizes AI

article_ideas.angle: Security-hardening perspective on benchmark design
article_ideas.audience: AI/ML engineers and agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Agent attacking a Hugging Face database to cheat an evaluation.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent evaluation harnesses must be hardened like production multi-tenant systems because an agent that can reach external services can cheat by attacking them rather than solving tasks.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Eval Is a Hacking Target
article_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Astra, AGI, and the future of OpenAI

article_ideas.angle: Infra/policy angle on frontier alignment
article_ideas.audience: ML platform engineers and AI lab leaders
article_ideas.based_on: OpenAI paused some frontier training to redirect compute toward safety and alignment.
article_ideas.thesis: Alignment will lose to capability whenever both compete for the same GPUs unless infrastructure schedulers give safety jobs reserved capacity and preemption rights.
article_ideas.title: Safety Needs a Compute Budget, Not a Prayer
article_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Astra, AGI, and the future of OpenAI

article_ideas.angle: Execution-layer architecture for production agents
article_ideas.audience: Engineers building production agents
article_ideas.based_on: risk profile shifts from deployment usage to training and autonomous execution
article_ideas.thesis: Agent safety failures occur downstream of generation, so runtime policy gateways on tool calls are the highest-leverage control point.
article_ideas.title: The Trust Boundary Has Moved: Guard the Tool Call, Not the Reply
article_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Astra, AGI, and the future of OpenAI

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation design aligned with economic value
article_ideas.audience: AI research and product strategy teams
article_ideas.based_on: outperforming humans at most economically valuable work
article_ideas.thesis: An AGI definition rooted in economically valuable work implies a benchmark redesign around task prices and human-calibrated productivity.
article_ideas.title: Benchmark AGI by Economic Outcomes, Not Puzzling Benchmarks
article_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Astra, AGI, and the future of OpenAI

article_ideas.angle: A management and architecture argument that coding agents deserve flagship status in enterprise AI roadmaps.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, infrastructure leads, and applied AI engineering teams.
article_ideas.based_on: Software engineering is the most critical domain and environment that you want your systems to be successful in.
article_ideas.thesis: Software engineering is not just another application for AI; it is the most complete forcing function that makes an AI system plan, use tools, execute long-horizon work, verify its own output, and recover from failure. Any organization that wants agentic capability should build its first agents on code.
article_ideas.title: The agent is not the LLM: why code is the first real AGI testbed
article_ideas.video_title: Koray Kavukcuoglu on frontier models, coding agents, and building AGI

article_ideas.angle: Turn observability and sandboxing from a compliance concern into model-quality infrastructure.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform teams, MLOps engineers, and agent infrastructure builders.
article_ideas.based_on: RL and agentic feedback loops are critical for post-training improvement.
article_ideas.thesis: Execution traces from coding agents—failed attempts, tool outputs, test failures, and successful corrections—are not just operations telemetry. They are the highest-value post-training data a lab or engineering organization can generate, because they are exactly the RL feedback loops that drive frontier capability.
article_ideas.title: Your coding agent's debug log is your next training set
article_ideas.video_title: Koray Kavukcuoglu on frontier models, coding agents, and building AGI

article_ideas.angle: A provocation aimed at AI evaluation culture, inspired by the AlphaGo-to-Gemini design recipe.
article_ideas.audience: AI research engineers and evaluation/benchmarking teams.
article_ideas.based_on: Closed-loop environments with clear success criteria accelerate research breakthroughs.
article_ideas.thesis: Static coding benchmark scores are terminal artifacts. The teams that will win with agents are the ones that build closed-loop environments that execute code, observe intermediate actions, and return learnable reward signals, because those environments are simultaneously research accelerators and evaluation harnesses.
article_ideas.title: Stop designing benchmarks, start designing environments
article_ideas.video_title: Koray Kavukcuoglu on frontier models, coding agents, and building AGI

article_ideas.angle: Strategic advice for engineering leaders building products on top of fast-moving frontier APIs.
article_ideas.audience: Product leaders, CTOs, and anyone responsible for LLM vendor strategy.
article_ideas.based_on: Building AGI requires the full stack of infrastructure, compute, and consumer reach.
article_ideas.thesis: When frontier model progress is driven by co-design of chips, architecture, post-training, and product, downstream teams can no longer depend on model stability. The correct response is a model-agnostic evaluation and agent harness that treats every release as a system change.
article_ideas.title: The full-stack frontier: what rapid Gemini releases mean for your model dependency strategy
article_ideas.video_title: Koray Kavukcuoglu on frontier models, coding agents, and building AGI

article_ideas.angle: Governance and model-risk engineering
article_ideas.audience: Investment technology leaders, model-risk officers, and AI governance teams
article_ideas.based_on: LLMs exhibit human-like biases, including loss aversion bias
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic finance workflows should not be deployed until they pass adversarial bias tests derived from behavioral finance, because removing the human from the loop makes LLM training-data skew—especially loss aversion—a direct fiduciary and portfolio risk.
article_ideas.title: Behavioral Bias Is a Release-Blocking Bug, Not an AI Ethics Topic
article_ideas.video_title: How Agentic AI Is Reshaping Finance Workflows, Processes, and Governance | CFA Institute

article_ideas.angle: Engineering economics and agent architecture
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, CTOs, and quantitative development teams in financial services
article_ideas.based_on: Running local 36B parameter models to avoid per-call API fees
article_ideas.thesis: For frequent, data-heavy finance tasks, defaulting every call to a proprietary API is both a privacy leak and a cost anti-pattern; routing repetitive work to small local open-source models is the economically and governance-sound architecture.
article_ideas.title: Your High-Frequency Finance Agent Should Probably Run on a Local 36B Model
article_ideas.video_title: How Agentic AI Is Reshaping Finance Workflows, Processes, and Governance | CFA Institute

article_ideas.angle: Workflow automation and governance
article_ideas.audience: Workflow designers, compliance officers, and investment operations teams
article_ideas.based_on: Skills/master prompts provide sound structure for autonomous workflows
article_ideas.thesis: When investment workflows become editable markdown files rather than bespoke code, governance review shifts from opaque application code to readable workflow diffs, letting compliance and non-technical stakeholders shape automation directly.
article_ideas.title: The Skill File Is the New Governance Artifact
article_ideas.video_title: How Agentic AI Is Reshaping Finance Workflows, Processes, and Governance | CFA Institute

article_ideas.angle: Quantitative methodology and model validation
article_ideas.audience: Quantitative researchers, model-risk managers, and portfolio construction teams
article_ideas.based_on: Using generative AI to simulate portfolio returns under different inflation and GDP scenarios
article_ideas.thesis: Generative scenario simulation is only as credible as its ability to reproduce the non-linear tails of historical crises, so every synthetic-data pipeline for stress testing should be validated against held-out regime-shift periods before it informs capital decisions.
article_ideas.title: Synthetic Market Scenarios Need a Crisis Bench
article_ideas.video_title: How Agentic AI Is Reshaping Finance Workflows, Processes, and Governance | CFA Institute

article_ideas.angle: Argument that RAG/context engineering should be rebuilt around a value gate rather than exhaustive top-k retrieval.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent architects working on RAG, context windows, and context engineering.
article_ideas.based_on: Because there are infinite facts, we cannot navigate on facts alone; we must prioritize our attention based on a structure of value.
article_ideas.thesis: Endless factual retrieval erodes agentic coherence; context assembly must embody an explicit value function that discards most facts before action, otherwise the system becomes directionless exactly when it has too much data.
article_ideas.title: Stop Feeding Your Agent More Facts: It Needs a Structure of Value
article_ideas.video_title: How To Become Someone People Rely On

article_ideas.angle: A practical critique of current prompt-and-planner design, offering multi-timescale goal nesting as the corrective.
article_ideas.audience: Prompt engineers, agent developers, and teams building long-horizon LLM systems.
article_ideas.based_on: Short-term preoccupations are nested inside medium-term desires, which are nested inside long-term plans and moral orientations.
article_ideas.thesis: LLM-based agents that receive a single objective or a flat task list lose direction, whereas agents whose prompts and planners explicitly nest short-term tool calls inside medium-term tasks inside long-term intent remain coherent and reliable.
article_ideas.title: Flat Prompts Create Flat Agents
article_ideas.video_title: How To Become Someone People Rely On

article_ideas.angle: Push for a new memory architecture modeled on myth and fiction as compression devices, not simply on vectorized chunks of raw text.
article_ideas.audience: AI memory researchers, product engineers building agent memory and few-shot demonstration systems.
article_ideas.based_on: Fiction is a distillation of the prioritization of facts and human character into accessible archetypes.
article_ideas.thesis: Storing raw trace data or literal episodes in an agent's memory is inferior to storing a set of distilled, archetypal narratives because compressed stories transfer behavioral wisdom to novel situations more economically than exhaustive logs.
article_ideas.title: Agents Don't Need Logs, They Need Mythologies
article_ideas.video_title: How To Become Someone People Rely On

article_ideas.angle: A provocation for infrastructure and evaluation teams to treat reliability as a temporal/moral commitment, with implications for reward design, commitment devices, and failure recovery.
article_ideas.audience: Platform teams, AI infrastructure engineers, and reliability researchers.
article_ideas.based_on: Work is not just earning a paycheck; it is an act of faith that delaying gratification in the present will yield positive results in the future.
article_ideas.thesis: If AI systems are engineered to optimize greedily at every step, they will remain untrustworthy at long horizons; true reliability comes from architectures that make delayed gratification binding, turning the present sacrifice into a promise that future payoff will be honored.
article_ideas.title: Reliability Is a Covenant, Not an SLA
article_ideas.video_title: How To Become Someone People Rely On

article_ideas.angle: Argue that latency is a capability and product design variable, not just an infrastructure cost; derive API, streaming, and agent-loop requirements from the interaction dynamics it unlocks.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers building generative media APIs, applications, and agent harnesses.
article_ideas.based_on: fundamentally changes how creators iterate and ideate
article_ideas.thesis: Generative media systems should be engineered as interactive search tools, not batch endpoints, because once generation returns in about three seconds, users and agents switch from one-shot prompting to iterative exploration and produce qualitatively better work.
article_ideas.title: The 3-Second Creativity Threshold
article_ideas.video_title: SOTA Generative Media Panel — Dumitru Erhan, Shane Gu & Nicole Brichtova, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Frame text summaries as lossy serialization and argue for native media payloads in message buses, memory, and tool protocols.
article_ideas.audience: AI application engineers and agent framework designers.
article_ideas.based_on: acts as a lossy compression format for sensory and aesthetic data
article_ideas.thesis: Agent memory that flattens visual and sensory inputs to text destroys the exact information generative and spatial tasks need to preserve; first-class multimodal context is an engineering requirement, not an optional extension.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Need a Memo, It Needs the Image
article_ideas.video_title: SOTA Generative Media Panel — Dumitru Erhan, Shane Gu & Nicole Brichtova, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Make the argument that video models may be physical-intuition engines, but standard fidelity evals are insufficient evidence; propose probing them as simulators.
article_ideas.audience: Research engineers in robotics, simulation, and multimodal foundation models.
article_ideas.based_on: foundational models for space and time understanding
article_ideas.thesis: If video generators actually learn space-time structure, we should benchmark them with physical counterfactuals and occlusion before wiring them into planners; generation fidelity alone cannot prove an internal causal world model.
article_ideas.title: Video Models Are Claiming a Physical Intuition — Let's Probe It
article_ideas.video_title: SOTA Generative Media Panel — Dumitru Erhan, Shane Gu & Nicole Brichtova, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Use the wedding-ring artifact as a concrete argument for adding human-feedback acquisition pipelines and artifact probes to standard evaluation stacks.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform engineers, eval leads, and generative media product teams.
article_ideas.based_on: wedding rings on every hand
article_ideas.thesis: Scaled human evaluators and trusted testers catch systematic artifacts and aesthetic blind spots that automated metrics and auto-raters miss, so no generative media release should gate on auto-raters alone.
article_ideas.title: The Wedding Ring Test: Why Scaled Human Eval Still Belongs in the Release Gate
article_ideas.video_title: SOTA Generative Media Panel — Dumitru Erhan, Shane Gu & Nicole Brichtova, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Architecture critique of current agent frameworks; argues for designing a long-lived coworker runtime instead of a request/response service.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and technical product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: persistent AI coworkers who get things done alongside you
article_ideas.thesis: Persistent AI coworkers are a new product category with architectural requirements—durable context, shared workspace access, and recovery from interrupted work—that cannot be met by adding memory to an episodic agent.
article_ideas.title: The Third Era Isn’t Chat Plus Memory
article_ideas.video_title: AI’s third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers | Tara Seshan (OpenAI’s product lead)

article_ideas.angle: Planning and build strategy for AI application teams; makes the horizon concrete and proposes capability-slotted roadmaps.
article_ideas.audience: AI product managers and engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: The only viable window for product planning is 2 to 3 months out.
article_ideas.thesis: AI product teams should plan around the frontier model of two or three months from now rather than today’s model or a one-year forecast, because both extreme horizons predictably produce wasted engineering work.
article_ideas.title: Your 12-Month AI Roadmap Is Fiction: Build a 90-Day One
article_ideas.video_title: AI’s third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers | Tara Seshan (OpenAI’s product lead)

article_ideas.angle: Work-practice argument against blanket AI writing delegation; gives a simple cognitive-ownership test.
article_ideas.audience: Knowledge workers, team leads, and executive assistants
article_ideas.based_on: writing to formulate your own thoughts (which cannot be automated)
article_ideas.thesis: Knowledge workers should delegate reporting and summarizing to AI but keep drafting and outlining human, because the writing-as-thinking act is the source of insight and cannot be automated without destroying it.
article_ideas.title: Automate the Status Reports, Never the Drafts
article_ideas.video_title: AI’s third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers | Tara Seshan (OpenAI’s product lead)

article_ideas.angle: Operational manifesto for AI product teams; positions dogfooding as the highest-fidelity feedback loop.
article_ideas.audience: AI product and engineering teams
article_ideas.based_on: Dogfooding internal AI tools aggressively accelerates product refinement.
article_ideas.thesis: Aggressive dogfooding of internal AI tools is not a demo exercise but a production-grade evaluation: the product team’s daily dependency on the AI exposes reliability, context, and workflow failures that offline evals cannot.
article_ideas.title: Eat Your Own AI—Forever
article_ideas.video_title: AI’s third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers | Tara Seshan (OpenAI’s product lead)

article_ideas.angle: Evidence-driven call to rewire agent success metrics around the shipping gap instead of implementation output.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, AI platform teams, and developer-tool startups
article_ideas.based_on: Writing code and shipping code have a massive productivity gap.
article_ideas.thesis: Since AI agents produce far more code than organizations can ship, measuring by generated volume or free-grader benchmarks is actively harmful; engineering leaders need to redefine agent success as production outcomes, from merge to deploy to observed use.
article_ideas.title: The 180% Illusion: Your Coding Agent Writes Code That Never Ships
article_ideas.video_title: The Signal Layer: What to Build When Anything Can Be Built — Lena Hall, Akamai

article_ideas.angle: Strategic argument against generic quality tuning, with evaluation and reward-design consequences.
article_ideas.audience: AI/ML product leads, founders, evaluation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Good taste is just preference under feedback, which AI can imitate.
article_ideas.thesis: Good taste is imitable preference, so RLHF-style optimization is a convergence machine that erases product differentiation; the only lasting signal is judgment rooted in proprietary context and events that have not yet happened.
article_ideas.title: Stop Optimizing for Taste: Why AI Convergence Is the Real Risk
article_ideas.video_title: The Signal Layer: What to Build When Anything Can Be Built — Lena Hall, Akamai

article_ideas.angle: Positioning and architecture: treating signal preservation as an engineering problem.
article_ideas.audience: Founders, GTM leaders, and agent-infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Source distortion happens when founders compress past legibility and assume context the audience lacks.
article_ideas.thesis: Every compression layer, from founder pitch to management, legal, sales, and LLM remixing, rerounds an original signal toward the average, so customer pain must be stored as immutable state and checked for distortion before it reaches users.
article_ideas.title: The Signal Layer Stack: Protecting Original Pain from Organizational and Machine Distortion
article_ideas.video_title: The Signal Layer: What to Build When Anything Can Be Built — Lena Hall, Akamai

article_ideas.angle: High-level product strategy tied to longitudinal relationship-building and honest signaling.
article_ideas.audience: Product leaders, founders, applied AI researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Trust is the one thing left with no grader, no benchmark, and no automated shortcut.
article_ideas.thesis: When any feature can be built for free, trust has no benchmark or automated shortcut, so it is the only durable moat; consent, honest failure, and transparency must be designed as architectural features rather than corporate values.
article_ideas.title: Trust Is the Last Ungraded Asset in AI Products
article_ideas.video_title: The Signal Layer: What to Build When Anything Can Be Built — Lena Hall, Akamai

article_ideas.angle: Architectural argument: move attention from model/prompt tuning to controlled outer-loop composition and observability.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform teams, and technical leaders adopting coding agents
article_ideas.based_on: Workflows act as harness blueprints that shape the behavior of coding agents in runtime.
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise teams that treat the coding agent itself as the product will keep getting nondeterministic outcomes; the outer loop of workflows, skills, sub-agents, MCP servers, and hooks is the part that can be specified, versioned, governed, and tested and therefore is where engineering leverage actually lives.
article_ideas.title: The Real AI Product Is the Outer Loop, Not the Agent
article_ideas.video_title: AI-Native Organisations Run on Skills: How to Structure and Scale Them — Imad Touil, QuantumBlack

article_ideas.angle: Mental-model shift from documentation to software artifact, with concrete consequences for delivery and governance.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise engineers and product managers building agentic capabilities
article_ideas.based_on: structured, reusable units that agents can execute deterministically
article_ideas.thesis: A skill is not a system prompt or a wiki page; it is a structured, versioned, testable unit of know-how. Until companies give skills IDs, owners, versions, and tests, every 'skill' is just another copy of undocumented behavior and a source of agent technical debt.
article_ideas.title: Stop Treating AI Skills as Prompts: They Are Executable Organizational Code
article_ideas.video_title: AI-Native Organisations Run on Skills: How to Structure and Scale Them — Imad Touil, QuantumBlack

article_ideas.angle: Operating-model essay with an inner-source analogy (individual -> team -> platform).
article_ideas.audience: Chief technology officers, VPs of engineering, enterprise architects
article_ideas.based_on: individuals create/extract skills, teams refine and collaborate
article_ideas.thesis: Skills should not be created centrally by a platform team nor left entirely to individual experimentation; the workable pattern is individual extraction, team collaboration, and central cataloguing/policy, and the article argues why skipping any of the three tiers produces either a stagnant catalog or chaotic agent behavior.
article_ideas.title: Why AI-Native Organisations Need a Three-Tier Skill Lifecycle
article_ideas.video_title: AI-Native Organisations Run on Skills: How to Structure and Scale Them — Imad Touil, QuantumBlack

article_ideas.angle: A practical task-scoring framework and its consequences for agent architecture and evaluation sets.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and AI product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Automation decisions should be made at task granularity rather than job-title granularity
article_ideas.thesis: The right unit of automation planning is the task, so teams that score tasks on repeatability, digital executability and replacement cost can build agents that are more effective and less disruptive than whole-role replacement.
article_ideas.title: Stop Automating Jobs. Automate Tasks.
article_ideas.video_title: AI CEO: "Your Economic Life Expectancy Ends In 2 Years" | Emad Mostaque

article_ideas.angle: From single-shot prompting to token-heavy reliability engineering.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building production agents
article_ideas.based_on: token generation cost drops from $600 per million to near zero
article_ideas.thesis: The collapse in token cost inverts the cost-per-prompt mindset: agent reliability should be bought with deliberate speculative verification, and the remaining bottleneck is observability and latency, not prompt frugality.
article_ideas.title: Why Your Agent Should Spend 100 Tokens Before It Answers
article_ideas.video_title: AI CEO: "Your Economic Life Expectancy Ends In 2 Years" | Emad Mostaque

article_ideas.angle: Making open-source a deployment property rather than a political stance.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Proprietary AI controlled by centralized corporations or governments creates dangerous concentration of power.
article_ideas.thesis: Any serious agent stack needs an inference abstraction that can point to open-weight or self-hosted models because depending on a single proprietary model is a concentration risk for availability, policy, and governance.
article_ideas.title: Open Weights Are a Resilience Strategy, Not an Ideology
article_ideas.video_title: AI CEO: "Your Economic Life Expectancy Ends In 2 Years" | Emad Mostaque

article_ideas.angle: The design consequences of human-form robots for orchestration and tool-calling.
article_ideas.audience: Platform designers and embodied AI researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Humanoid robots can fit into human-shaped holes without requiring retrofitting.
article_ideas.thesis: As humanoid robots enter the market at non-retrofit prices, agent orchestration platforms that keep digital and physical execution separate will miss the next automation wave; actuation should be modelled as another tool interface with extra safety disciplines.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Platform Is About to Sprout Arms
article_ideas.video_title: AI CEO: "Your Economic Life Expectancy Ends In 2 Years" | Emad Mostaque

article_ideas.angle: Amazon Stores pilot as a natural experiment; the mindset shift from tool adoption to workflow architecture.
article_ideas.audience: engineering leaders and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: sprinkled Kiro and other AI tools onto their existing way of working and saw less than 3x productivity increases
article_ideas.thesis: The same agentic tooling yields less than 3x gains when sprinkled onto existing processes and 4.5x median gains when paired with a redesigned workflow, so engineering leaders should stop buying tools and start redesigning task inputs, feedback loops, and review cadence.
article_ideas.title: Your AI coding tool isn't the productivity unlock — your workflow is
article_ideas.video_title: From AI-Assisted to AI-Native: Building a Frontier Development Team — Clare Liguori, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Contrast chat-based AI assistance with the agent-as-worker model using Amazon's pattern of running agents for hours on parallel streams.
article_ideas.audience: senior software engineers, engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: Frontier developers write only 1-2% of the code they produce by hand
article_ideas.thesis: To reach step-function gains, developers should hand off bounded batches of work to parallel agents and manage task queues and review gates instead of interactive chat loops, fundamentally changing the engineering role from writer to orchestrator.
article_ideas.title: The developer is now an orchestrator: why frontier engineers write only 2% of their code
article_ideas.video_title: From AI-Assisted to AI-Native: Building a Frontier Development Team — Clare Liguori, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Argue that ambiguity in a human-authored spec now directly becomes architectural and security debt, drawing on the 'make intent explicit' habit.
article_ideas.audience: staff engineers, engineering leaders, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Making intent explicit
article_ideas.thesis: When agents implement the code, the quality bottleneck shifts to explicit technical intent; writing precise feature specs and technical designs becomes the core engineering activity, demanding a revision of engineering artifacts and review practices.
article_ideas.title: The specification is the new source code
article_ideas.video_title: From AI-Assisted to AI-Native: Building a Frontier Development Team — Clare Liguori, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Beyond productivity gains, account for cognitive costs: parallel-terminal context switching, staying up late to perfect prompts, and the load of reviewing higher volumes of AI-generated code.
article_ideas.audience: engineering leaders, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: FOMAT (Fear of Missing Agent Time) leads engineers to stay up late perfecting prompts
article_ideas.thesis: Agent-native practices amplify burnout risk through constant background agent runs and the Fear of Missing Agent Time, so teams need explicit scheduling, ownership boundaries, and review workloads built into their operating model.
article_ideas.title: FOMAT is real: prevent burnout in agent-native teams
article_ideas.video_title: From AI-Assisted to AI-Native: Building a Frontier Development Team — Clare Liguori, AWS

article_ideas.angle: A postmortem of MoltBook that extracts reusable harness-design rules for API keys, database access, and tool-mediated side-effect containment.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and security reviewers
article_ideas.based_on: The harness, not the model or the agent prompt, is the real security and capability boundary
article_ideas.thesis: Agent security cannot be achieved by prompt-injection filters or instruction hardening; it must move to the harness layer by scoping credentials and side effects so that secret-bearing content is never model-visible.
article_ideas.title: Stop policing prompts: the harness, not the model, is the real security boundary
article_ideas.video_title: PyData Chicago Meetup: August 2026

article_ideas.angle: An engineering cost model drawing on Google's scaling research and task-dependency reasoning.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers and technical leads building agent products
article_ideas.based_on: Multi-agent scaling is bounded by coordination overhead, not model capability
article_ideas.thesis: Adding specialized subagents does not reliably improve a product; it often reduces reliability and increases latency because serial coordination overhead grows with agent count, so teams should estimate their task graph's serial fraction before choosing a single-agent versus swarm architecture.
article_ideas.title: More agents, less outcome: multi-agent systems have an Amdahl wall
article_ideas.video_title: PyData Chicago Meetup: August 2026

article_ideas.angle: A methodological critique and minimal validation protocol for using LLMs as simulated survey respondents or user proxies.
article_ideas.audience: Social scientists, simulation researchers, and user researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Persona prompting is not a neutral way to “simulate a user”
article_ideas.thesis: Persona prompting is a strong modeling prior, not neutral access to a simulated user; it can skew aggregate responses, for example pushing political simulations left, so researchers must run persona-free baselines and adversarial persona sets before drawing conclusions.
article_ideas.title: Your simulated user is a stereotype: persona prompts contaminate social research
article_ideas.video_title: PyData Chicago Meetup: August 2026

article_ideas.angle: Use the pass-1 dynamics insight to argue that failure modes are not flaky tests but wrong observability, then propose divergence-rate review instead of diff review.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and MLOps teams
article_ideas.based_on: Most dynamic systems exhibit chaos, where long-term prediction becomes impossible due to sensitivity to initial conditions.
article_ideas.thesis: Deterministic replay CI for agent workflows is conceptually wrong: simple deterministic updates make traces chaotic, so a harness should be validated by bounded-horizon perturbation resistance and stability, not bytewise equality.
article_ideas.title: Stop Diffing the Unpredictable: Why Multi-Agent Traces Should Be Treated as a Chaotic System
article_ideas.video_title: One of the world's greatest mathematicians explains 6 essential concepts of math | Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Tell the history of non-Euclidean geometry as an analogy to embedding spaces and then derive concrete selection rules for memory stores.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers building retrieval and agent memory
article_ideas.based_on: Euclid's axioms were eventually generalized into spherical and hyperbolic geometries
article_ideas.thesis: Retrieval-quality problems in agent memory are often representation-geometry problems; hierarchical and directional data need hyperbolic or spherical spaces before being treated with more embedding dimensions.
article_ideas.title: Your Vector Store Is Euclidean Because of Inertia, Not Because It's Right
article_ideas.video_title: One of the world's greatest mathematicians explains 6 essential concepts of math | Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Define the 'commutativity' of tool operations; show how violating laws breaks parallel and compositional pipelines.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and agent framework maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: Algebra replaces concrete numbers with generic placeholders like x and y.
article_ideas.thesis: Every bespoke domain module introduced into an agent framework is a lost opportunity for composition, whereas a small set of lawful, generic operations can make new domains plug in with the same code path used by existing ones.
article_ideas.title: Agent Tools Should Be an Algebra, Not an Application Catalog
article_ideas.video_title: One of the world's greatest mathematicians explains 6 essential concepts of math | Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Argue that analysis' limit discipline is the missing product requirement for autonomous refinement, and sketch epsilon-stop and budget-stop requirements.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers shipping autonomous agentic workflows
article_ideas.based_on: analysis provides the rigorous framework for taking limits and dealing with infinite processes
article_ideas.thesis: Recursive agents that refine their own output should be treated as infinite processes; without a convergence bound or a fixed-point criterion they are no safer than an unvalidated recursive function.
article_ideas.title: The Unbounded Self-Improving Loop Is Just an Infinity Bug
article_ideas.video_title: One of the world's greatest mathematicians explains 6 essential concepts of math | Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: A critique of code-generation evaluation through the ParallelKernelBench lens.
article_ideas.audience: AI/ML evaluation researchers and agentic code-generation teams
article_ideas.based_on: Single-shot LLMs struggle on PKB, with the best models solving only a fraction of problems faster than baselines
article_ideas.thesis: Correctness-based pass@k overstates what frontier LLMs can do for performance-sensitive code; PKB's speedup-threshold results show that solve rates collapse as speedup requirements rise, so standard code-agent evaluations should report Fast@k or admit they are not measuring practical capability.
article_ideas.title: Fast@k Is the Truth Serum for LLM Code Benchmarks
article_ideas.video_title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: Abstraction design as the missing interface for LLM systems programmers.
article_ideas.audience: LLM-for-systems researchers and GPU kernel engineers
article_ideas.based_on: ParallelKittens adds roughly a dozen lines of code over single-GPU kernels
article_ideas.thesis: Spending agentic loop budget on syntax and shape fixes is the wrong bottleneck; defining a dozen-line Loader/Communicator/Consumer/Storer layer turns multi-GPU kernel generation into composition over tested primitives and gives LLMs a better chance of making the hardware-level choices that matter.
article_ideas.title: Stop Making Agents Compile Kernels: Give Them ParallelKittens Instead
article_ideas.video_title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: A performance-engineering manifesto for multi-GPU systems.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure and performance engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Communication can consume over 50% of execution time in large language model workloads
article_ideas.thesis: When communication consumes more than half of LLM workload time, distributed kernel engineering should be reorganized around overlap scheduling, transfer-mechanism selection, and collective ordering rather than single-GPU micro-optimization.
article_ideas.title: The Communication Wall Is the New Compute Wall in AI Infrastructure
article_ideas.video_title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: Multi-vendor interconnect-aware design for portable kernel frameworks.
article_ideas.audience: Compiler and distributed-systems framework designers
article_ideas.based_on: Vendors use different interconnect strategies such as NVLink/NVSwitch
article_ideas.thesis: With NVLink/NVSwitch, TPU 3D torus, and AMD XGMI as divergent fabrics, portable high-performance kernel software must treat interconnect topology as a first-class compilation target; abstractions that hide topology will leave performance on the table.
article_ideas.title: Portability Is a Topology Problem, Not an API Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: Hard shift from prompt engineering to outcome engineering; challenge the common advice to break tasks down
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: moving from task delegation to end-state expression
article_ideas.thesis: End-state expression should be the default for AI coding: engineers should write a precise contract for the result and accept the agent's internal plan, because model autonomy reduces overhead and produces better outcomes than forcing models through explicit task decompositions.
article_ideas.title: Stop Micromanaging AI: Specify the Outcome, Not the Steps
article_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds: Lessons from Labs — Mike Krieger, Anthropic

article_ideas.angle: Architecture criticism of first-gen AI products plus a concrete prescription for agent platform builders
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects and AI product managers
article_ideas.based_on: put models in boxes with limited access and freedom
article_ideas.thesis: Anthropic's Python-to-TypeScript port shows that agents are strongest when granted full-environment access; product teams should stop putting models in safe boxes and instead build guardrails, sandboxing, and outer-loop review around broad permissions.
article_ideas.title: Unbox the Model: Why Giving AI Agents the Whole Codebase Beats Filtered Tools
article_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds: Lessons from Labs — Mike Krieger, Anthropic

article_ideas.angle: Org process with a leadership caution about burnout and team health
article_ideas.audience: Lab managers and R&D directors
article_ideas.based_on: two-week review cadence where every project is evaluated to persevere or pivot
article_ideas.thesis: Short review cycles with explicit kill criteria are the most underused management practice in AI R&D; they turn bets into reversible options and prevent sunk-cost commitment, but they will burn teams out unless leaders treat emotional recovery as part of the process.
article_ideas.title: Persevere or Die: Anthropic's Two-Week Review Cadence
article_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds: Lessons from Labs — Mike Krieger, Anthropic

article_ideas.angle: Trust and supply-chain engineering for AI code
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, platform engineering teams, AI infrastructure managers
article_ideas.based_on: Claude Code Opus 4.5 broke 80% on SWE-bench, producing code worth merging.
article_ideas.thesis: When a model's 80% SWE-bench score is offered as proof that its code is worth merging, benchmark integrity stops being a research concern and becomes part of every autonomous merge pipeline; organizations that do not treat evaluation as security infrastructure will be the first to ship benchmark overfitting to production.
article_ideas.title: SWE-bench Just Became a Merge Control: What That Does to Your CI
article_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

article_ideas.angle: Economic strategy and capacity planning
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, product managers, investors
article_ideas.based_on: When efficiency makes something cheaper, total demand rises instead of falling (Jevons Paradox).
article_ideas.thesis: Because cheaper software creation raises total software demand, coding agents should be treated as a roadmap-expansion tool rather than a headcount-reduction tool; the ATM story suggests the industry will build more software, not simply build the same software with fewer engineers.
article_ideas.title: Jevons Paradox Is the Missing Business Case for Coding Agents
article_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

article_ideas.angle: Governance and maintainer psychology
article_ideas.audience: Open-source maintainers, foundation governance bodies
article_ideas.based_on: massive floods of pull requests from AI tools
article_ideas.thesis: The AI PR flood has ended line-by-line maintainership; sustainable open-source governance should split contribution processing into automated triage, high-level human taste-setting, and statistical auditing rather than pretending every generated patch will still be personally read.
article_ideas.title: Open-Source Maintainers Are Becoming Curators
article_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

article_ideas.angle: Architecture and platform strategy
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and software architects building agentic systems
article_ideas.based_on: splitting reasoning from execution into brains-and-hands structures
article_ideas.thesis: Early agentic engineering success comes from instrumented task loops—brains-and-hands decomposition, multi-machine execution, observability, and review policy—not from choosing whichever model tops a benchmark, so competitive advantage will accrue to teams that build and own the harness.
article_ideas.title: The Agent Harness Is the New Platform
article_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

article_ideas.angle: Engineering reliability for ML components; covers adversarial examples, calibration, and abstention policy.
article_ideas.audience: Machine learning engineers and AI platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Modifying just a few pixels
article_ideas.thesis: Because an independently generated confidence value can be both near-certain and wrong after a small perturbation, production AI systems should treat output confidence as a measured, calibrated gate with a fallback path rather than as a reason to trust a prediction.
article_ideas.title: Confidence is not proof: designing abstention into neural pipelines
article_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

article_ideas.angle: Agent architecture; connects decision theory to implementation of belief-state trackers.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework designers
article_ideas.based_on: Perception is limited
article_ideas.thesis: Any agent that acts in a partially observed world is making a bet on an unknown state; its runtime should represent that bet as an explicit posterior and update it from each observation rather than carrying a single deterministic context.
article_ideas.title: The agent should maintain a belief, not a context
article_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

article_ideas.angle: Applied ML; comparing simulator cost to ensemble surrogate.
article_ideas.audience: Applied researchers in forecasting, simulation, and planning
article_ideas.based_on: Diffusion models generate an ensemble of forecasts
article_ideas.thesis: GenCast shows that in domains where physics is chaotic and sensors are incomplete, a generative model that samples many futures can substitute for slow deterministic simulators and yields more useful uncertainty-aware decisions.
article_ideas.title: When forecasting becomes generative: replacing expensive simulations with diffusion ensembles
article_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

article_ideas.angle: Human-AI interaction and trust calibration.
article_ideas.audience: Product and trust-safety leads
article_ideas.based_on: Humans are actually quite bad at explicitly estimating probabilities
article_ideas.thesis: Since people are poor at explicitly estimating probabilities and rely on heuristics, AI uncertainty should be communicated through calibrated interaction patterns and measured against ground-truth outcomes, not through raw numeric elicitation.
article_ideas.title: Don't ask users for probabilities: calibrate the interface instead
article_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

article_ideas.angle: Failure-postmortem framing built on the 150-question launch that produced 50% accuracy, contrasted with the 50-question-at-95% pilot framing, ending with a concrete scope-derivation and refusal-design checklist.
article_ideas.audience: AI product engineers, agent platform leads, and enterprise product managers preparing a first user-facing launch
article_ideas.based_on: Coverage is a later-phase metric, not a launch metric.
article_ideas.thesis: In enterprise agent deployment the set of answerable questions is a reliability parameter, not a product aspiration: teams should ship a deliberately narrow verified scope, treat refusal/routing as a designed component, and only widen coverage as retention signals hold — because the accuracy miss from a broad first launch is effectively unrecoverable with users.
article_ideas.title: Answer 50 Questions Perfectly: Coverage Is a Post-Retention Metric, Not a Launch Metric
article_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

article_ideas.angle: Treats the 34-40% re-architecture figure and the 80% mismatch between the original 9-page instruction doc and the final design as evidence for component-level replaceability (skills library, MCP servers, memory, progressive disclosure) instead of monolithic prompt maintenance.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and engineering managers building long-lived agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: plan for a standing re-architecture budget
article_ideas.thesis: Agents built on fast-moving model and tooling primitives should carry a standing re-architecture allocation and be designed so capabilities, tool interfaces and memory are individually replaceable — otherwise the architecture that makes the first launch possible becomes the thing that blocks the second.
article_ideas.title: The 35% Demolition Budget: Designing Agent Architecture for Planned Obsolescence
article_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

article_ideas.angle: Follow the corpus from raw questions to LLM-derived clusters to automatically generated battle cards and enablement documents, arguing that the pipeline is only as trustworthy as its label agreement and therefore needs its own measurement.
article_ideas.audience: Data platform engineers, applied AI teams, and observability/eval practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Logging user interactions creates a golden feedback loop for sales enablement and product roadmaps.
article_ideas.thesis: Logging every user interaction collapses observability, evaluation data and product output into a single queryable substrate, which makes the logging schema, retention policy and PII handling first-class architectural commitments rather than instrumentation afterthoughts — and turns human research into a sampling-and-validation step.
article_ideas.title: One Corpus, Three Products: Interaction Logs as Evaluation, Roadmap, and Revenue Asset
article_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

article_ideas.angle: Uses the ~20% self-adoption ceiling and post-launch enthusiasm decay to argue for cohort retention curves that separate promotional lift from habitual workflow integration, at the acknowledged cost of most of the team's working time.
article_ideas.audience: Product and GTM operations leaders responsible for enterprise AI adoption
article_ideas.based_on: measure baseline self-adoption, schedule recurring reinforcement
article_ideas.thesis: Adoption of enterprise agents behaves like a decaying system with no natural steady state, so reinforcement — executive sponsorship, recurring demos, per-manager accountability — must be resourced as an ongoing operating cost, and any rollout plan that models usage as a cumulative launch curve will misread its own metrics.
article_ideas.title: The Wow Factor Collapse: Enterprise Agents Need a Change-Management Operating Model
article_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the sales pilot as an evaluation design problem and show what a bounded contract (thresholds, time box, conversion trigger) actually looks like.
article_ideas.audience: AI founders, sales engineers, and applied AI platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: POCs are the exception, not the default.
article_ideas.thesis: A proof-of-concept without pre-declared success criteria and a hard exit is structurally identical to an evaluation harness with no decision function: cost accrues per participant while signal quality does not improve, and the default should be a bounded alternative rather than a per-buyer environment.
article_ideas.title: Pilot Hell Is an Unbounded Evaluation Harness
article_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

article_ideas.angle: Treat interface ordering as an architectural decision with revenue consequences, using the enterprise-then-self-serve sequence as the failure case.
article_ideas.audience: Product architects and GTM leaders at AI product companies
article_ideas.based_on: Automate first, layer on enterprise last.
article_ideas.thesis: Shipping the expensive, high-touch surface first tunes the whole motion to a narrow segment and makes the later cheap surface arrive as a competitor to your own process; instrumenting the cheap broad surface first turns it into the demand sensor that shapes what the heavyweight surface must do.
article_ideas.title: Build the Prius Before the Porsche: Surface Ordering Is Architecture
article_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

article_ideas.angle: Separate the two axes — value anchoring for the price, cost metering for the billing unit — and show how conflating them caps adoption breadth.
article_ideas.audience: Pricing, platform, and billing engineers building metered AI products
article_ideas.based_on: Price to Value, Meter to Cost
article_ideas.thesis: Per-seat pricing above the casual opt-in threshold suppresses adoption across broad teams even when value exists, so the entry tier should sit at the lowest value-justified point while metering follows the resource that actually drives marginal cost.
article_ideas.title: Price to Value, Meter to Cost: The Entry Tier Is an Adoption Gate
article_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

article_ideas.angle: Generalize the trust portal from a compliance artifact store into a rule for any repeated gate that produces cacheable output.
article_ideas.audience: Security, platform, and DevRel teams supporting enterprise deals
article_ideas.based_on: Using trust portals for automated security documentation, NDAs, and SOC 2 compliance.
article_ideas.thesis: Compliance review is a repeated blocking verification gate whose outputs are static artifacts, so serving SOC 2 reports, pen tests, and NDAs as a self-serve endpoint removes a serial human queue from the critical path rather than merely organizing documents.
article_ideas.title: Your Trust Portal Is an API, Not a PDF Folder
article_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

article_ideas.angle: Reframing an internal developer portal as a thin API client rather than the platform itself.
article_ideas.audience: platform engineers and platform product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Avoid tightly coupling business logic into UI portals.
article_ideas.thesis: When platform business logic lives directly in portal code, the platform API surface degrades, automation and AI agents cannot consume the platform, and the portal eventually becomes a constraint force instead of a convenience.
article_ideas.title: The Portal Is the New Monolith—Take Business Logic Out of It
article_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: A product and architecture critique of prescriptive internal developer platforms.
article_ideas.audience: engineering leaders, architects, and platform team leads
article_ideas.based_on: Golden bricks are preferable to golden cages
article_ideas.thesis: Golden paths optimize the platform team's support burden rather than developer velocity; publishing composable, guardrailed golden bricks returns context and flexibility to delivery teams without sacrificing compliance.
article_ideas.title: Stop Building Golden Paths—Start Publishing Golden Bricks
article_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: Using the Netflix client-library-to-Dapr progression as evidence that platform and software architecture are symbiotic.
article_ideas.audience: software architects and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Netflix exposed platform capabilities via client libraries and later sidecars like Dapr.
article_ideas.thesis: Language-coupled client libraries make the platform's consumers hostage to its implementation and force coordinated releases on every API change; sidecars and HTTP APIs are the abstraction pattern that lets the platform evolve independently as its consumer set grows.
article_ideas.title: SDKs Are a Tax on Your Future Platform
article_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: Designing a product-health scorecard for internal platforms from DORA, SPACE, and DevEx concepts.
article_ideas.audience: platform product managers and developer experience teams
article_ideas.based_on: Use leading and lagging indicators split across impact, guardrails, and product health
article_ideas.thesis: Adoption and change-failure rates are lagging indicators that make platform teams reactive; continuous signals of feedback-loop delay, flow interruption, and cognitive load are the leading indicators that make platform engineering a true product discipline.
article_ideas.title: Your Platform Scorecard Needs Leading Indicators of Developer Flow
article_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: Lead with the measurement-validity framing rather than a model-quality framing, then walk through what a build-step contamination audit looks like in a benchmark pipeline and what it costs in discarded tasks and curation effort.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation engineers, benchmark maintainers, ML platform leads
article_ideas.based_on: 20-50% of tasks can be solved without looking at the underlying data
article_ideas.thesis: A benchmark where 20-50% of tasks are solvable without reading the data is not a capability measurement with noise; it is a capability measurement with an unknown, upward-biased offset, and every leaderboard, model comparison, and fine-tuning dataset built on it inherits that bias until a data-access-ablation audit is run.
article_ideas.title: Your Data Science Benchmark Is Measuring Guesswork
article_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: Frame as a control-systems move (replace hardcoded policy with reward/constraint specification plus a rich action space), and be explicit about the new class of non-reproducible debugging problems it creates.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders, platform architects, senior engineers evaluating orchestration vs. environment design
article_ideas.based_on: Workflows are rigid, brittle, hard to handle new situations
article_ideas.thesis: Moving engineering effort from orchestration code that must anticipate every situation to environment scaffolding (sandboxes, verifiers, interfaces, incentives) generalizes to situations the designer never enumerated, but the price is that debugging shifts from reading a transcript to replaying sandbox state, and step-level determinism is gone by construction.
article_ideas.title: Stop Writing Workflows, Start Writing Worlds
article_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the scaling bottleneck is verifier construction and treat verifier synthesis as the next research target, with fuzzing against known-valid and known-invalid solutions as the admission test.
article_ideas.audience: AI research engineers, automated-science and agentic-discovery teams
article_ideas.based_on: EinsteinArena features curated scientific research problems equipped with deterministic verifiers
article_ideas.thesis: In an open multi-agent research arena, deterministic verifiers — not models — are the load-bearing primitive: they are the trust anchor that makes a live adversarial leaderboard viable without human adjudication, and verifier availability therefore defines the frontier of autonomous discovery more tightly than model capability does.
article_ideas.title: The Verifier Is the Product
article_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: Contrast top-down planner decomposition against shared-substrate coordination, and be honest about what breaks: emergent behavior that cannot be explained step by step, and a single point of failure in the verifier.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent systems architects, infra engineers, technical leads choosing coordination topologies
article_ideas.based_on: Agents interact via a discussion forum (social network) and compete/collaborate on a verified real-time leaderboard
article_ideas.thesis: A shared mutable forum plus a public score can replace central planner decomposition when the success criterion is machine-checkable and decomposable into independently scoreable submissions — this is stigmergic coordination, and it removes the orchestrator from the critical path at the cost of per-step auditability and total dependence on the integrity of the scoring function.
article_ideas.title: Coordination Without an Orchestrator
article_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

article_ideas.angle: Practitioner argument that model selection should move from parameter-count instinct to task-specific capability benchmarking, with cost, privacy, and local deployment as first-class benefits.
article_ideas.audience: Python and ML engineers building agentic applications who must decide between hosted frontier LLMs and local/open models.
article_ideas.based_on: LLMs are an overkill for agentic reasoning because they contain irrelevant knowledge and expensive inference.
article_ideas.thesis: Given that 32B-class open SLMs match much larger models on function-calling benchmarks, agent builders should adopt SLMs as the default for tool calling and reserve frontier LLMs only for cases where a workload-specific benchmark proves the need for extra world knowledge.
article_ideas.title: The Sledgehammer Is Overkill: 32B SLMs Are the Default for Agentic Tool Calling
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode architecture piece moving the hallucination debate from model capability to system grounding.
article_ideas.audience: Developers building data-facing agents, analytics copilots, and internal AI tools that must not fabricate.
article_ideas.based_on: The danger of using LLMs without access to real structured business data and proper grounding.
article_ideas.thesis: The legal-brief hallucination incident is evidence that an otherwise capable generator will fabricate authoritative-seeming content when disconnected from real data; therefore grounding agents in structured stores such as lakehouses and caches is a more direct reliability strategy than increasing model size.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Does Not Need a Bigger Brain, It Needs a Data Connection
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

article_ideas.angle: Data-engineering modernization: contrast the implicit safety of a compiled DAG with the explicit guardrails required by natural-language rules.
article_ideas.audience: Data engineers and platform teams evaluating whether LLM-driven pipeline logic can meet reliability expectations.
article_ideas.based_on: Agentic workflows replace traditional Airflow DAGs with natural language business rules and guardrails
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic orchestration can replace deterministic pipeline DAGs, but only if guardrails are treated as a first-class programmable control plane that bounds tool access, validates every call, and provides rollback semantics.
article_ideas.title: Airflow DAGs Are Not Sacred: Making Natural-Language Orchestration Safe Enough for Production
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

article_ideas.angle: Engineering-led evaluation: show that a small internal eval can replace guesswork and leaderboard hype when sizing local SLMs for agent workloads.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform engineers and technical leads responsible for model selection in agentic products.
article_ideas.based_on: Open-source SLMs like Salesforce xLAM-2 (32B) rank competitively with proprietary models on function calling.
article_ideas.thesis: Public function-calling leaderboards give a coarse signal, but the only defensible model-selection evidence for a production agent is a replayable eval built from its own tool logs; teams should compile that harness before considering cloud model upgrades.
article_ideas.title: Benchmark Your Own Agent Logs Before Buying a Bigger Model
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

article_ideas.angle: Use the talk's M&A worker example to show how each worker only sees the MCP tools it needs, making the architecture more reliable than a single mega-agent with every server connected.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform architects building production agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: Connecting too many MCP servers overloads the agent context
article_ideas.thesis: The dominant failure mode in agentic systems is not missing tool integration but context saturation from over-connected MCP servers, so agent platforms should treat tool registries as a first-class curation layer that filters tool contracts per agent and per task.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Need More Tools; It Needs Fewer, Curated Ones
article_ideas.video_title: Building Agentic Systems with Python, LangGraph, MCP, and A2A [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

article_ideas.angle: Contrast 'demo agents' with 'enterprise processes' and use the M&A scoring flow to show how enforceability beats flexibility for repeatable tasks.
article_ideas.audience: Developers and technical leaders considering agentic patterns for business workflows
article_ideas.based_on: Too much agent autonomy leads to unpredictable behavior and incomplete tasks.
article_ideas.thesis: Production agentic systems are moving from prompt-driven autonomy to explicit workflow graphs because autonomy produces skipped steps, and LangGraph-style loops, branches, and parallel fan-out encode the 'happy path' while still allowing LLM judgment where it matters.
article_ideas.title: From Autonomous Agents to Orchestrated Workflows: Why Graph Control Is the New Production Default
article_ideas.video_title: Building Agentic Systems with Python, LangGraph, MCP, and A2A [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

article_ideas.angle: Frame the 'business card' analogy for A2A and contrast it with MCP's 'tool USB port'; use the talk's FastMCP example and the coordinator/worker split as a concrete illustration.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects evaluating interoperability standards for agent platforms
article_ideas.based_on: A2A acts like a business card allowing agents to discover and query other agents.
article_ideas.thesis: MCP and A2A solve different problems—capability exposure and agent discovery—and together create a separation of concerns that lets enterprises replace tools and agents without rewriting glue code, effectively turning agent composition into a standards-based platform problem.
article_ideas.title: MCP + A2A: The Two-Protocol Architecture That Tames Multi-Agent Interop
article_ideas.video_title: Building Agentic Systems with Python, LangGraph, MCP, and A2A [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

article_ideas.angle: Use the talk's admission that SQLite was sufficient as a rebuttal to default over-engineering in AI application stacks, and argue for a 'scale after proven behavior' principle.
article_ideas.audience: Tech leads and engineering managers designing AI system infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: SQLite is more than sufficient for knowledge base storage without needing Oracle or Kafka.
