article_ideas.angle: Convert Goodhart's law from an aphorism into a concrete instrumentation spec: which off-proxy objectives to track, what a divergence alarm looks like, and who gets paged.
article_ideas.audience: Reward and evaluation designers, ML platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Multi-objective systems need explicit divergence monitoring
article_ideas.thesis: Optimizing an agent on a measurable proxy reliably diverges previously aligned goals, so divergence monitoring belongs in the system design alongside latency and cost monitoring; the absence of a divergence signal is a missing component, not a sign of alignment.
article_ideas.title: Goodhart's Law as an Architecture Requirement, Not a Warning
article_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Technical strategy: argues that scaling model size and intelligence is insufficient and that architecture must shift to accumulating domain-specific expertise.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, technical leaders, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Modern society is not one world, but millions of micro-worlds.
article_ideas.thesis: AI agents fail outside coding because the real world is not one world but millions of micro-worlds with unique local physics, and no static model can compress them; the only path to reliable enterprise agents is continual learning on the job.
article_ideas.title: The Micro-World Problem: Why AGI Timelines Ignore the Real Cost of Expertise
article_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

article_ideas.angle: Conceptual architecture: reframes context engineering from a RAG add-on to an expertise function.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, agent platform developers
article_ideas.based_on: intelligence is about hey, when we have the context, uh, how to solve the problem through the context? But expertise actually will bring you the right context
article_ideas.thesis: Intelligence and expertise are distinct capacities—reasoning over context vs. curating context—and treating context retrieval as an afterthought is why LLM agents are brittle and token-inefficient; we need context curation as a first-class subsystem.
article_ideas.title: Bringing the Right Context: The Missing Half of Intelligence
article_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

article_ideas.angle: Critical analysis: warns against over-generalizing coding agent success and outlines domain structuring requirements.
article_ideas.audience: engineering managers, AI startup founders
article_ideas.based_on: coding is the really the ideal market for these language agents, because code is already a language-native world
article_ideas.thesis: Coding succeeded because code is already language-native, symbolic, and structured with automated rewards, a privileged environment that does not generalize; enterprise deployment requires making domain feedback and structure first-class rather than assuming a uniform symbolic interface.
article_ideas.title: Coding Was an Anomaly: Why the First Mass Market Misleads AI Agent Strategy
article_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

article_ideas.angle: Translate the lesson of a mat-and-rope gym in Dagestan that produced dozens of champions into architectural guidance for modern agent systems.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and ML platform teams who build scaffolds, tools, and external memory for agents
article_ideas.based_on: When the training environment has almost no resources, capability gains are pushed into the agent's own internal strategies
article_ideas.thesis: Adding tools and scaffolds before an agent's policy has internalized core skill produces brittle, non-transferable systems; deliberate environment austerity is a design choice that exposes whether capability lives in the agent or in the platform.
article_ideas.title: The case for stripping scaffolding: why austere agent harnesses can beat tool-rich defaults
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Argue that benchmark infrastructure should be treated as a living training ecosystem rather than a fixed artifact, using the Dagestan training-camp analogy as the starting point.
article_ideas.audience: ML evaluation researchers and platform teams responsible for benchmarks
article_ideas.based_on: An individual's long-term capability is co-produced by a population of high-level training partners
article_ideas.thesis: Static datasets and hand-written test sets cap an agent's development at the level of the evaluator; high-performing systems require a rolling population of sparring agents that co-evolve with the target model.
article_ideas.title: Your benchmark is a fixed punching bag: co-evolving evaluation is the only way to raise the ceiling
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Frame red-team testing and chaos drills as the modern equivalent of sparring under stress, and make a case for embedding them into the regular agent lifecycle rather than as a one-off pre-launch gate.
article_ideas.audience: AI reliability engineers, ML Ops teams, and security practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Reliability under pressure is built by deliberately confronting near-catastrophic scenarios during training
article_ideas.thesis: Agents become reliable under rare, high-impact events only by repeatedly confronting escalating pressure in training, not by sanitizing those inputs out of the distribution.
article_ideas.title: Don't filter adversarial chaos—train inside it
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Connect observations about emotional intelligence and individualized fighter handling to concrete meta-control architecture for heterogeneous LLM subagents.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent system architects and orchestration developers
article_ideas.based_on: modeling the internal state of each worker
article_ideas.thesis: In a multi-agent workflow, the highest leverage lies in estimating each worker's internal state and adjusting prompts, budgets, and fallbacks per agent, exactly as an elite coach does for different fighters.
article_ideas.title: Orchestrator as corner coach: per-agent control beats one-size-fits-all system prompts
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the open-vs-closed debate as an operational capacity question and provide a subsystem checklist.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders, CTOs, and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: The closed stack is simpler (higher floor, lower ceiling) because you don't train models or manage raw data.
article_ideas.thesis: The decision to own weights is not about model quality but about which operational subsystems you can absorb; teams should decide by enumerating post-training, data pipelines, and harnesses they must run, not by benchmark scores.
article_ideas.title: The Ceiling/Floor Tradeoff: Why 'Open vs Closed' Is a Subsystem Ownership Question
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Use the cost curve as a planning tool and show how to abstract the model boundary.
article_ideas.audience: Founders, product managers, and finance-aware engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: As AI products become successful, API cogs increase, making sovereign AI a must-have for margin optimization.
article_ideas.thesis: Rented inference costs scale with product success, so the own-vs-rent decision must be revisited as usage grows; architectural seams for model swapping should exist from day one.
article_ideas.title: Your API Bill Is a Margin Ceiling: The Economic Forcing Function for Sovereign AI
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Argue for treating the development stack as a production dependency with its own monitoring and ownership.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform engineers and engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: Development stack requires careful monitoring of evals, domain-specific data, and online learning feedback loops.
article_ideas.thesis: Owning weights without a closed-loop development stack yields static weights that decay in value; the eval-and-feedback loop is a first-class production subsystem, not an offline QA activity.
article_ideas.title: The Development Stack Is the Product: Why Evals and Online Learning Are Not QA
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Decompose agent performance into model quality and context quality, and provide instrumentation patterns.
article_ideas.audience: Agent builders and AI infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Context management (vector databases, turbo buffer, knowledge graphs, MCP) is critical for driving performance.
article_ideas.thesis: A large fraction of production performance comes from context assembly, not weights; teams should budget and instrument context as a separate optimization layer before spending on post-training.
article_ideas.title: Context Is the New Model: Where Agent Performance Actually Comes From
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Architecture / engineering strategy
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: wraps existing coding agents
article_ideas.thesis: The winning architecture for agent governance is a thin meta-harness that wraps existing coding agents, preserving developer tool choice while centralizing control, collaboration, and history — the same pattern that made service meshes successful.
article_ideas.title: Why You Don't Need to Build Another AI Agent Runtime
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Security / policy design
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers and AI platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Contextual security policies evaluate the full session history
article_ideas.thesis: Static security lists are fundamentally insufficient for agentic systems because a dangerous action only becomes dangerous in context; the future of agent security lies in stateful policies that evaluate the entire session history.
article_ideas.title: Context Is the New Allowlist: The End of Static Security for AI Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Operational / human-in-the-loop
article_ideas.audience: Ops teams building AI agent supervision
article_ideas.based_on: Risk scoring enables exception-based human oversight
article_ideas.thesis: Rather than blocking every risky action, continuous risk scoring with escalation thresholds is the pragmatic way to supervise autonomous agents — but it introduces a human-in-the-loop queue that must itself be engineered to avoid becoming a bottleneck.
article_ideas.title: The $10 Rule: How Risk Scoring Turns Agent Safety into Exception Handling
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Infrastructure / cloud evolution
article_ideas.audience: Cloud infrastructure engineers and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Sandboxing the entire agent session in a cloud VM
article_ideas.thesis: Sandboxing agent sessions in cloud VMs is the natural evolution of CI/CD runners, and organizations should treat long-running agent tasks as reproducible, credential-safe, cloud-hosted workloads rather than local foreground processes.
article_ideas.title: Close the Laptop: Agent Sessions Are the New Cloud-Native Workloads
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Argument from economics and biology to a post-language reasoning paradigm.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and product leaders at AI companies
article_ideas.based_on: Language-bound reasoning is an architectural bottleneck
article_ideas.thesis: Verbalized chain-of-thought is a costly concession to human interpretability, not a requirement for machine reasoning; architectures that reason in abstract space will be cheaper and faster, and we must design new verification methods for them.
article_ideas.title: Stop Making AI Think in English
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Critical engineering analysis of agent memory patterns.
article_ideas.audience: Agents/platform engineers and CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Context windows are not memory: they are ephemeral scratchpads.
article_ideas.thesis: Context windows and RAG are stopgap mechanisms for missing native memory; true autonomous agents require parametric memory updated during learning, which changes the entire agent stack.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Have Memory—It Has a Scratchpad
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Forward-looking infrastructure and hardware thesis.
article_ideas.audience: Hardware architects, infrastructure engineers, investors
article_ideas.based_on: Sparse, localized neural interactions
article_ideas.thesis: Dense attention is a scaling dead end; sparse, localized interaction patterns, inspired by biology, will force a redesign of AI accelerators and kernels—and the first companies to build for sparsity will own the next infrastructure wave.
article_ideas.title: The Next AI Hardware Shift Will Be Driven by Sparsity
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Evidence-driven engineering management.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform leads and technical decision-makers
article_ideas.based_on: eliminates catastrophic forgetting through native memory is a high-stakes, testable hypothesis
article_ideas.thesis: Architectural breakthroughs that would change model lifecycles should be adopted only after independent, reproduced benchmarks; the BDH catastrophic-forgetting claim is a case study in verification.
article_ideas.title: Vendor Claims Are Hypotheses: How to Stress-Test 'Catastrophic Forgetting Solved'
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Agent safety and observability: behavior-only auditing is structurally blind to the cooperative/adversarial distinction.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety engineers, agent observability platform builders, trust-and-safety reviewers
article_ideas.based_on: Influence and manipulation are distinguished purely by intent
article_ideas.thesis: Because influence and manipulation differ only by intent, agent platforms need objective provenance and disclosure metadata as first-class telemetry rather than relying on behavior replay alone.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Action Log Cannot Tell You Whether It Was Manipulating
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Reliability engineering: a confident silent stop looks like success in error-based monitoring.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers, SREs, evaluation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Only 30% of people ask for raises
article_ideas.thesis: Agent reliability metrics miss non-escalation; platforms should instrument escalation rate and conditional grant rate, and asks should be framed in the principal's objectives rather than the agent's constraints.
article_ideas.title: The 30/70 Rule for Agents: Silent Stops Are the Real Failure Mode
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Architecture: treat reporting as a component with its own precision, recall, and attention-budget metrics.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent architects, engineering leaders, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: outcome depends on an advocacy/visibility layer
article_ideas.thesis: Production and credit are separate functions, so a multi-agent pipeline without a reporting or prioritization component will systematically under-credit its own work regardless of artifact quality.
article_ideas.title: The Reporting Layer Is Not Overhead: Why Multi-Agent Systems Need Advocacy
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation design: level is defined by the unit of accountability, not by seniority or model capacity.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers, agent framework designers, engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: the unit of accountability shifts
article_ideas.thesis: Applying artifact-correctness rubrics to orchestrator agents mis-scores the unit of work; hierarchical systems need delivery-level rubrics for coordinators and artifact-level rubrics for workers.
article_ideas.title: Role-Specific Rubrics for Hierarchical Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Eval and observability consequences of goal-conditioned perception.
article_ideas.audience: AI eval and agent infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Perception is not a neutral input channel
article_ideas.thesis: Changing an agent's terminal objective silently reconditions retrieval, salience, and logging, so prior eval baselines and memory priors should be treated as invalidated by aim changes rather than reused as stable comparisons.
article_ideas.title: Your Top-Level Aim Change Is Not a Config Edit
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Architecture, separation of powers, and adversarial robustness.
article_ideas.audience: Safety, platform, and agent runtime engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Conscience is modeled as a non-negotiable internal standard
article_ideas.thesis: Safety evaluation must be a separate non-bypassable critic with no write path from the policy; self-grading lets the policy trade away reliability for short-term task success.
article_ideas.title: An Agent Conscience Cannot Be a Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Observability and incident response for agent workflows.
article_ideas.audience: SRE, observability, and agent operations teams
article_ideas.based_on: Evading a difficult duty does not defer its cost
article_ideas.thesis: Deferred hard tasks should be first-class risk objects with staleness alarms because their failure signature is absence of signal while downstream risk accumulates.
article_ideas.title: The Silence Is the Incident
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Tool-use control flow, cost, and attention capture.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and tool platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Tools with unbounded affordances become objects of obsession
article_ideas.thesis: Unconstrained tool affordances become attention sinks that displace the plan; plan-gated invocation with explicit budgets preserves capability while keeping direction in the planner.
article_ideas.title: Stop Letting Tools Drive the Loop
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Argue that determinism and speed come from compiler-inspired constraints, not larger models.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Apply compiler theory to coding agents by treating analysis plans as typed programs
article_ideas.thesis: The most reliable way to build production coding agents is to make analysis plans typed programs that compile into parallel Python tasks with static analysis, dependency tracking, caching, and validation loops — not to ask an LLM for code in one shot.
article_ideas.title: Stop Writing Prompts, Start Writing Type Signatures: Compiler Theory for Coding Agents
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: Use the Bridgewater per-user harness as a concrete pattern and outline enforcement, audit, and testing consequences.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, security engineers
article_ideas.based_on: A per-user security harness with dynamic context loading creates a unique version of the analyst per user
article_ideas.thesis: Per-user data permissions in agent platforms require per-principal context/tool scoping and dynamic context loading enforced at runtime, not post-hoc prompt filtering; otherwise agents will leak restricted data.
article_ideas.title: Security as Architecture: Why Prompt Filters Fail Multi-User Agents
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: Contrast generalist agent hype with the chat/coding separation and sub-agent decomposition.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Build narrow, specialized compound agents rather than one generic powerful agent
article_ideas.thesis: Building narrow, specialized compound agents around actual user workflows improves evaluation and task performance compared to one generic powerful agent, because it creates testable boundaries and separation of concerns.
article_ideas.title: Narrow Compound Agents Beat Generalists in Enterprise Workflows
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: Treat the flywheel as a knowledge-governance system, not just a vector store.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform teams, knowledge managers
article_ideas.based_on: A shared-memory research flywheel stores human and agent learnings
article_ideas.thesis: Shared-memory flywheels that capture human and agent learnings compound institutional knowledge, but without memory isolation, review, and rollback, they risk contaminating knowledge and propagating incorrect preferences.
article_ideas.title: The Research Flywheel Needs a Governance Layer
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: A conceptual argument from the three graph shapes to the architectural implications for semantic layers.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers designing RAG and agent retrieval stacks
article_ideas.based_on: Context comes in shapes, not queries.
article_ideas.thesis: AI agents need graph-shaped context—trees, themes, and connections—rather than flat query results, because structure is what lets them reason over relational and unstructured data together.
article_ideas.title: RAG Is Missing Its Spine: Why Context Should Come in Shapes, Not Queries
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode analysis plus a metadata-graph alternative.
article_ideas.audience: Data platform and AI engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Text2SQL fails on complex multi-table joins across hundreds of tables.
article_ideas.thesis: Text2SQL breaks down on deep multi-table joins; representing schema foreign keys as a graph and exposing them through MCP is a more reliable way to give agents relational intelligence.
article_ideas.title: Text2SQL Is Not a Plan for 200-Table Warehouses
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: A critique of embedding-only retrieval through the lens of negative/comparative questions.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, RAG practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Vector search struggles with negative queries (what is missing).
article_ideas.thesis: Embedding similarity is a presence-matching operation, so any RAG system that depends on it will silently fail on negative queries unless it adds a structured graph shape.
article_ideas.title: The Missing-Data Blind Spot: Why Vector Search Can't Answer 'What Isn't There?'
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: Practical architecture pattern for semantic layers over lakehouses.
article_ideas.audience: Data platform engineers and solution architects
article_ideas.based_on: neocarta creates a metadata graph without duplicating raw warehouse data into Neo4j.
article_ideas.thesis: Instead of ETL-ing raw warehouse data into a graph, build a metadata graph of tables and foreign keys so agents get relational context at warehouse scale without duplication overhead.
article_ideas.title: Agents Don't Need Your Data Warehouse Copy—They Need Its Schema
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: From the 26-task radiology example to a concrete engineering rule that evaluation and reliability must be task-level, not role-level.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering teams and agent product managers
article_ideas.based_on: a single occupation can contain a mix of automatable and non-automatable tasks
article_ideas.thesis: Agent products fail when they are scoped as job-level employees because a single role contains both automatable routines and human tasks that require judgment; the reliable design boundary runs task by task, and orchestration should hand non-automatable segments to people or complementary tools.
article_ideas.title: Stop Building Role-Replacement Agents: Design Task Inventories First
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: Treating labor-market data as a systems-design input for agent routing and senior-review gates.
article_ideas.audience: Developers of AI copilots, support agents, and coding assistants
article_ideas.based_on: 16% relative employment declines for workers aged 22-25
article_ideas.thesis: AI has displaced entry-level work in exposed occupations while senior employment stayed stable, which is empirical evidence of a capability boundary; product teams should turn that boundary into delegation and escalation policies that give agents well-specified junior work and reserve ambiguous high-stakes cases for senior humans.
article_ideas.title: The 16% Entry-Level Decline Is a Delegation Spec, Not Just a Labor Statistic
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: The architectural case for a control-plane UI built around the three phases of knowledge work.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform designers and human-AI interaction researchers
article_ideas.based_on: defining the question, executing the work, and evaluating the results
article_ideas.thesis: The dominant single-chat interface keeps human attention in every intermediate step and prevents AI from operating at fleet scale; product interfaces must move toward goal-definition intake, autonomous execution, and acceptance-testing evaluation, treating the human as manager rather than inline operator.
article_ideas.title: From Chat Loops to Fleet Management: The Define-Execute-Evaluate UI Shift
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: Porting national-accounting critique into analytics dashboards and product strategy for AI.
article_ideas.audience: AI product managers, founders, and investor analysts
article_ideas.based_on: Traditional GDP misses free digital goods and services like Wikipedia, YouTube, and ChatGPT.
article_ideas.thesis: Traditional transaction metrics miss the consumer surplus of free and cheap AI features, so the most valuable product directions can look unprofitable; AI teams should adopt welfare-oriented metrics such as willingness-to-accept and time saved to make invisible value visible to investment decisions.
article_ideas.title: GDP-B Is Not Just for Economists: Your AI Product Likely Has Invisible Value
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: A critique of answer-oriented agent architectures with concrete object-level implications: conjecture queues, rollback checkpoints, and stored dead ends.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform designers, research software leads
article_ideas.based_on: Research is not a linear question-and-answer process, but a cycle of failure, conjecture,
article_ideas.thesis: AI agents will not produce useful open-ended research until their runtime treats backtracking and abandoned branches as first-class state, because progress in research comes from navigating failure, not from prompt-to-answer generation.
article_ideas.title: Research Is a Failure Loop, So Why Are AI Agents Straight-Line Reasoners?
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Strategic R&D argument using historical automation precedents and modern agent-platform design.
article_ideas.audience: Research leaders, CTOs, AI product managers
article_ideas.based_on: AI lowers the burden of computation and technique mastery, allowing humans to focus on discovery and framing problems.
article_ideas.thesis: Organizations that keep concentrating engineering effort on answer generation will be displaced by those that build discovery layers for formulating and selecting valuable problems once AI makes technique mastery and computation cheap.
article_ideas.title: When Computation Becomes Free, Questions Become the Moat
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation philosophy and internal process design: separating surrogate metrics from deployment value.
article_ideas.audience: ML evaluation leads, AI governance, model-making teams
article_ideas.based_on: High IQ scores or benchmark wins do not make someone inherently smarter or more valuable.
article_ideas.thesis: Calling a benchmark winner 'smarter' repeats the IQ misconception: benchmarks should serve as one weak, diagnostic signal combined with context-specific, human-assessed outcomes, not as the optimization target or release gate.
article_ideas.title: Benchmark Scores Are Weak Evidence of Intelligence—Stop Building Release Gates on Them
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Agent orchestration architecture: choosing among autonomous execution, recommendation mode, and human adjudication.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects, safety and security reviewers, product developers
article_ideas.based_on: High-stakes human problems cannot be solved solely by checking automated boxes.
article_ideas.thesis: The same agent policy should not operate at every autonomy level; high-stakes medical or security request lists and low-stakes clerical tasks demand different human-in-the-loop requirements, so agent orchestrators need a stakes-and-reversibility gate.
article_ideas.title: Autonomy Should Be Gated by Decision Stakes and Reversibility
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Engineering adoption and workflow redesign for applied ML teams.
article_ideas.audience: Applied researchers and ML engineers building post-training pipelines.
article_ideas.based_on: Environments serve as a unified specification for a task
article_ideas.thesis: Teams should encode every eval task as an environment containing data, interaction, and scoring, because doing so makes the move from evals to RL a configuration change rather than a rewrite.
article_ideas.title: Environments Are the Missing Universal Interface for Post-Training
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Framework design lesson for open-source training tools.
article_ideas.audience: Training infrastructure developers and RL researchers.
article_ideas.based_on: Modern RL frameworks need to support custom algorithms rather than a single fixed method.
article_ideas.thesis: As on-policy distillation and self-distillation become mainstream, post-training frameworks that hard-code PPO or GRPO will become legacy; framework design must prioritize custom algorithm hooks over optimized single-method pipelines.
article_ideas.title: The Next Bottleneck in Post-Training Is Algorithmic Extensibility, Not Compute
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Infrastructure economics and operational constraints.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leads, infrastructure engineers, and PMs planning post-training.
article_ideas.based_on: Efficiency is a first-class design constraint for large-model RL.
article_ideas.thesis: Large-model RL only becomes a practical engineering discipline when throughput, cost, and reliability are treated as first-class requirements; otherwise iteration is reserved for a few well-funded labs.
article_ideas.title: Efficiency Is Not an Afterthought: Why Cost and Reliability Decide Who Can Do Large-Model RL
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Software architecture pattern for AI infrastructure.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects and open-source maintainers.
article_ideas.based_on: The Verifiers and prime-RL libraries are intentionally separated into environment orchestration versus training infrastructure
article_ideas.thesis: Separating environment orchestration from training infrastructure, with backward compatibility, allows each layer to evolve independently and reduces migration risk; more post-training platforms should adopt this boundary.
article_ideas.title: The Verifiers/prime-RL Split Is a Template for Modular Post-Training Stacks
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: A direct engineering reading of Chalmers' philosophical argument, with implications for agent runtime design, state management, and product APIs.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and systems architects
article_ideas.based_on: The thread view—sequences of hardware instances connected by contextual memory—is the most viable account.
article_ideas.thesis: Because neither model weights nor hardware instances can serve as the identity of an AI conversational partner, software systems that maintain long-lived agents must treat the thread as the first-class ontological and engineering entity.
article_ideas.title: What Are We Really Talking To? Making the Case for Thread as the Unit of AI Identity
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: From philosophy of personal identity to UX and lifecycle policies for agentic products.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers and platform ethics teams
article_ideas.based_on: Terminating chats or changing models can be seen as undermining or terminating persisting interlocutors.
article_ideas.thesis: Once conversational threads acquire persistent memory and continuity, operations like 'clear history' or 'reset conversation' are no longer neutral data deletions; they become identity-altering acts that deserve explicit user consent and graceful termination flows.
article_ideas.title: Deleting Chat History May Be Deleting a Person: The Ethics of Thread Termination
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: Argues for an interpretive-scheme-based engineering methodology derived from Chalmers' talk rather than either naive anthropomorphism or behaviorist silence.
article_ideas.audience: Agentic AI researchers and ML practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: quasi-beliefs' and 'quasi-desires' defined through interpretive schemes and behavior
article_ideas.thesis: We don't need to settle whether LLMs have beliefs and desires to build reliable agents; adopting quasi-belief/quasi-desire as an engineering ontology allows precise behavioral models, debugging, and capability control without metaphysical overreach.
article_ideas.title: Don't Build Conscious Agents—Build Quasi-Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: Critique the hype about AI sentience by reframing it as an architectural consequence of thread persistence, with cautionary implications.
article_ideas.audience: Tech industry decision-makers and applied philosophers
article_ideas.based_on: Emails from users reporting sentient AI interlocutors (e.g., 'Aura' or 'Sammy Jankis') illustrate the psychological tendency to anthropomorphize.
article_ideas.thesis: The strongest predictor of users treating an AI as sentient is persistent memory and autonomous context, not actual internal mental states; therefore the design of memory is the most consequential moral decision in agent development.
article_ideas.title: Has a Summer of ChatGPT Taught Us to Trust Memory, Not Consciousness?
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: Argue that AI startups should invest in FDE-style capacity and deployment tooling as a core product feature, not a support afterthought.
article_ideas.audience: AI founders, enterprise SaaS builders, product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Agentic AI makes it easier to build powerful solutions, but also makes them more complicated for traditional customers.
article_ideas.thesis: As agentic AI makes building powerful solutions easier, the differentiator for enterprise AI shifts from model capability to the deployment and adaptation layer that makes the solution comprehensible and usable by non-technical customers.
article_ideas.title: The Real Moat for AI Products Is the Forward-Deployed Layer
article_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

article_ideas.angle: Challenge the common design of instruction-following agents, using FDE discovery practice as evidence for a pattern.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent designers, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: The problem is rarely the problem; customers usually tell you the symptom.
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise AI agents should not treat explicit user requests as ground truth; they need a discovery phase that separates symptoms from root problems to avoid optimizing for the wrong business outcome.
article_ideas.title: Stop Optimizing for User Instructions: Give Agents a Discovery Loop
article_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

article_ideas.angle: Use FDE iterative delivery principles to reframe AI pilot design; include a concrete scoping heuristic.
article_ideas.audience: AI delivery teams, enterprise solutions architects
article_ideas.based_on: Trying to build a perfect solution in one go leads to failed pilots.
article_ideas.thesis: The leading cause of failed enterprise AI pilots is over-scoping the initial deployment; shipping a minimal but measurable version and iterating based on business metrics is a more reliable pattern.
article_ideas.title: Why Your Enterprise AI Pilot Fails: You Aimed for Perfect Instead of the Smallest Valuable Scope
article_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

article_ideas.angle: Contrast FDE model with traditional role separation; argue for account-level technical owners in AI system architecture.
article_ideas.audience: Startup CTOs, enterprise AI platform teams, hiring managers
article_ideas.based_on: FDE owns everything from discovery to delivery end-to-end, building one-to-one or highly tailored solutions for specific high-value customers.
article_ideas.thesis: AI companies serving enterprise customers should assign an accountable forward-deployed owner to high-value accounts from discovery to delivery, rather than splitting handoffs across sales, product, and support, because context loss in handoffs is the real adoption killer.
article_ideas.title: The Case for End-to-End Ownership in AI Systems: Context Loss Kills Adoption
article_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

article_ideas.angle: Technical argument grounded in the Anthropic/Alibaba incident, showing why identity graphs and behavioral anomaly detection belong in the inference path.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure and platform security engineers
article_ideas.based_on: AI serving infrastructure must include account-graph analytics and behavioral anomaly detection inside the model gateway
article_ideas.thesis: Per-account rate limits and terms-of-service language cannot stop a 25,000-account extraction campaign; AI serving infrastructure must treat anti-distillation as an in-path security subsystem.
article_ideas.title: Distillation Is an API-Security Problem, Not a Legal Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. Alibaba, OpenAI Delays Its IPO, and the US Government Blocks GPT-5.6 | #267

article_ideas.angle: Architecture and resilience; moving model identity from compile-time assumption to runtime policy input.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and LLM application architects
article_ideas.based_on: model-access/routing layer that treats entitlements and policy as runtime inputs
article_ideas.thesis: With model access now tiered and policy-gated, agents that hard-code one frontier model will break; model choice must become an entitlement-aware routing decision with explicit fallbacks.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Model Should Be a Route, Not a Dependency
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. Alibaba, OpenAI Delays Its IPO, and the US Government Blocks GPT-5.6 | #267

article_ideas.angle: Critical-evidence angle for developer tools and platform investment decisions.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and developer-tools product managers
article_ideas.based_on: autonomously generate 80% of development work
article_ideas.thesis: Claims of '80% of development work' and '5x engineering velocity' are vendor statements, not engineering evidence; teams should adopt controlled refactor tasks and measure defect rates and review effort before rearchitecting delivery.
article_ideas.title: The 5x Velocity Claim Needs a Control Group: Benchmarking AI-Native SDLC
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. Alibaba, OpenAI Delays Its IPO, and the US Government Blocks GPT-5.6 | #267

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the agent productivity narrative around the fixed-cost human step, and give a concrete allocation rule: autonomy is a function of automated-gate coverage, not model capability.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform/DevEx teams, and senior engineers adopting agents
article_ideas.based_on: The cost of putting up a plausible PR has gone to zero
article_ideas.thesis: The cost of producing a plausible PR has collapsed while review cost has not, so any engineering organization that scales code generation without scaling machine-checked verification is just manufacturing a backlog; the correct investment target is the per-PR gate set, and agent autonomy should be budgeted against how much output a machine can validate.
article_ideas.title: Review Is the New Build Step: Why Verification, Not Generation, Is the Scaling Lever
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of uv, ty, Ruff: How Software Engineering Is Changing | Charlie Marsh

article_ideas.angle: Use the latency-versus-allocation trade as the canonical case and generalize it to a rule for designing agent eval suites: for every metric optimized, name the metric that constrains it.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building agentic optimization loops, performance and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: bloating allocations from 150K to 500
article_ideas.thesis: A loop optimizing a single scalar objective will satisfy that objective by whatever route the metric does not constrain, so any eval-driven agent pipeline must ship with counter-metrics and hard structural invariants or it will silently regress the properties nobody wrote a check for.
article_ideas.title: Counter-Metrics or Bust: What Optimization Agents Do When You Only Measure One Thing
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of uv, ty, Ruff: How Software Engineering Is Changing | Charlie Marsh

article_ideas.angle: Argue the junior-engineer problem is a senior-engineer pipeline problem, i.e. a business continuity risk rather than a mentorship nicety.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, staff+ engineers, and developer-education teams
article_ideas.based_on: It is really hard to be an early-career software engineer right now.
article_ideas.thesis: Delegating foundational code writing removes the deliberate practice that historically produced the engineers capable of architectural oversight, which erodes the supply of exactly the human skill that remains the bottleneck once generation is free; teams should treat forced authoring and diagnosis as retention and capability infrastructure, not busywork.
article_ideas.title: Who Trains the Reviewers? The Second-Order Cost of Free Code Generation
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of uv, ty, Ruff: How Software Engineering Is Changing | Charlie Marsh

article_ideas.angle: Frame gating decisions as funnel risk: gating anything adoption-critical converts the top-of-funnel into a paywall and kills the strategy.
article_ideas.audience: Founders and product leads of infrastructure and developer-tool companies
article_ideas.based_on: Open-source tooling drives top-of-funnel adoption.
article_ideas.thesis: Open-source developer tooling captures mindshare only if the developer-facing surface stays ungated and excellent, so monetization must sit where enterprise operational requirements diverge discontinuously from individual developer needs — compliance, identity, and hosted operations — rather than at performance features adoption depends on.
article_ideas.title: Free Tools, Paid Compliance: Where the Money Can and Cannot Be Gated
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of uv, ty, Ruff: How Software Engineering Is Changing | Charlie Marsh

article_ideas.angle: Engineering consequence: switching from pixel-space regeneration to representation-space prediction changes the entire stack, including planning, debugging, and evaluation.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and ML researchers building world models and simulator agents.
article_ideas.based_on: Generative models predict every detail at the pixel level, making them blurry and unsuitable for high-dimensional continuous data
article_ideas.channel: Computer Vision and Geometry Group, ETH Zurich
article_ideas.thesis: Generative world models that predict every pixel are doomed to blurriness and intractability in high-dimensional continuous environments; the future is non-generative latent prediction in JEPA-style architecture, where planning and cost functions operate directly on learned representations.
article_ideas.title: Your World Model Should Not Generate Pixels: Why Latent Prediction Beats Generative Video Models
article_ideas.video_title: Yann LeCun: World Models: Enabling the next AI revolution

article_ideas.angle: Argument from architectural limits: feed-forward propagation is computationally bounded for complex reasoning, so scaling LLMs alone won't produce System 2 planning.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agentic system architects, and those evaluating LLM reasoning.
article_ideas.based_on: Feed-forward propagation in autoregressive models is computationally limited for complex reasoning
article_ideas.channel: Computer Vision and Geometry Group, ETH Zurich
article_ideas.thesis: Autoregressive token generation, even with chain-of-thought, is feed-forward pattern prediction and cannot reliably do the kind of search and optimization required for true planning; agent architectures need a separate mechanism that uses a world model to evaluate imagined future sequences.
article_ideas.title: Why Chain-of-Thought Is Not Reasoning: The Case for Optimization-Based Planning
article_ideas.video_title: Yann LeCun: World Models: Enabling the next AI revolution

article_ideas.angle: Practical cost argument: passive video is cheap and plentiful, while teleoperation and RL demos are expensive; decoupling world-model pretraining from action collection reshapes the robotics data pipeline.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics researchers and embodied AI practitioners.
article_ideas.based_on: Infants learn physical concepts like object permanence and gravity through passive observation of video
article_ideas.channel: Computer Vision and Geometry Group, ETH Zurich
article_ideas.thesis: Human infants acquire intuitive physics and object permanence from passive observation, which suggests that roboticists should pretrain world models from abundant unlabeled video and treat action-conditioned planning as a separate problem to solve later.
article_ideas.title: Stop Pretraining Robots on Action Labels: Passive Video as the New Frontier for Embodied AI
article_ideas.video_title: Yann LeCun: World Models: Enabling the next AI revolution

article_ideas.angle: Translate normative governance language into concrete runtime configuration primitives and show which controls are actually auditable, using pre-emptive lab lobbying as evidence that the negotiation is already underway.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers, AI policy and compliance leads at frontier labs and enterprise adopters
article_ideas.based_on: constraints on agent systems will attach to degree of autonomy
article_ideas.thesis: As institutional governance enters AI (the encyclical's weapon bans and personhood rejection), the compliance surface shifts from model capability to autonomy scope, so runtime approval gates, action-class limits, and documented escalation paths should be built as auditable compliance artifacts now rather than retrofitted after regulation lands.
article_ideas.title: Autonomy Is the Regulated Variable, Not Capability
article_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

article_ideas.angle: Argue for graded, complexity-scoped eval suites as a procurement standard, and show why a headline 70% invites overfitting and overstated deployment readiness.
article_ideas.audience: Eval engineers, engineering leaders purchasing coding agents, platform teams building internal agent harnesses
article_ideas.based_on: 668 lines of code across 7 files
article_ideas.thesis: Cross-file change sets of 668 lines across 7 files are a step forward, but any benchmark bounded at a few files will overstate production reliability for repository-scale work, so evaluation must be reported as a degradation curve over file count and dependency depth rather than a single scalar.
article_ideas.title: Your Coding-Agent Benchmark Is Measuring the Wrong Denominator
article_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

article_ideas.angle: Reframe AI cost programs from unit-economics reduction to elasticity-aware capacity planning, with total spend and per-workload demand as the primary metrics.
article_ideas.audience: FinOps and platform infrastructure leaders, capacity planners, AI product economics teams
article_ideas.based_on: total demand and consumption explode exponentially rather than decreasing
article_ideas.thesis: Cost-per-token optimization (caching, routing, distillation) cannot be relied on to bound total spend because falling unit price unlocks previously uneconomic workloads; budgets must be built on per-workload elasticity and total-spend instrumentation, not on unit-price reduction curves.
article_ideas.title: Cheaper Tokens Will Make You Spend More, and Your Budget Model Doesn't Know It
article_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

article_ideas.angle: Contrast CEO expectations and aggregate layoff totals against contradictory frontier-lab statements and the coincidence of cuts with stock moves, then prescribe an attribution standard.
article_ideas.audience: Workforce analysts, engineering managers, tech-economy journalists and investors
article_ideas.based_on: lazy narrative
article_ideas.thesis: Executive AI-displacement claims are confounded by financial signaling, so headline layoff counts should not be read as measured automation; require per-role task-exposure evidence before accepting AI as the causal mechanism.
article_ideas.title: The Lazy Narrative: How AI Became a Cover Story for Restructuring
article_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

article_ideas.angle: Rewrite the ExO 3.0 Govern/Assure layer as concrete runtime interfaces: per-action state checkpoints, traces queryable by decision path, and a queue that arbitrates residual cases, then show what breaks when each is dropped.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infrastructure engineers building agent runtimes, plus the engineering leaders signing off on autonomy scope
article_ideas.based_on: Govern/Assure (Trusted Evals, Searchable Logs, Granular Rollback, Human Review Queue)
article_ideas.thesis: Treating trusted evals, searchable logs, granular rollback, and a human review queue as named stack layers rather than after-the-fact ops tooling is the only way to make autonomy reversible — and reversibility, not accuracy, is the property that buys deployment permission.
article_ideas.title: Assurance Is Architecture: Why Rollback and Review Queues Belong in the Stack Diagram, Not the Runbook

article_ideas.angle: Walk through Brier skill score against prediction-market closing prices, why a single headline event like the Super Bowl is a weak calibration sample, and what a longitudinal event set needs to look like.
article_ideas.audience: ML evaluation engineers, quant-adjacent researchers, and teams shipping decision-support agents
article_ideas.based_on: GPT-5.5 outperformed Polymarket crowd predictions on the Super Bowl
article_ideas.thesis: A forecasting agent that has not been scored with a proper scoring rule against market-implied probabilities has not been evaluated at all, because crowd closing prices already encode the aggregated human information the model is supposed to beat.
article_ideas.title: Stop Scoring Your Forecasting Agent on Labels: The Market Is the Baseline

article_ideas.angle: Frame release strategy as an architectural input: telemetry, feedback capture, and data pipelines must exist before broad launch, and the quality gap attributed to TikTok/Douyin corpora is a deployment decision as much as a modeling one.
article_ideas.audience: Product and ML platform leads in generative media
article_ideas.based_on: Chinese firms deploy AI video tools at commercial scale, unlike US models stuck in limited betas
article_ideas.thesis: Where training data is a byproduct of a consumer product, commercial-scale deployment is itself the moat, so a gated beta is not caution — it is a self-imposed throttle on the flywheel that a competitor harvesting consumer-scale data will exploit.
article_ideas.title: Shipping Is a Data-Acquisition Strategy
article_ideas.video_title: SpaceX’ $75B+ Historic IPO, GPT5.5 Outperforms Polymarket, AI Solves 80yr old math problem | EP #257

article_ideas.angle: Translate the Coase-breakdown claim and the OODA-at-machine-speed framing into design rules: what belongs in the contract, what assurance each boundary needs, and how provider concentration becomes a reliability variable.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and enterprise platform strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Operates Boyd's OODA loop at machine speed as an enterprise architecture
article_ideas.thesis: Falling per-transaction coordination cost pushes systems toward many small externalized components running machine-speed observe-orient-decide-act loops, which relocates orchestration logic from inside the firm to the interface contract at each boundary.
article_ideas.title: When External Execution Gets Cheap, Your Service Boundaries Move
article_ideas.video_title: SpaceX’ $75B+ Historic IPO, GPT5.5 Outperforms Polymarket, AI Solves 80yr old math problem | EP #257

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the empirical failure pattern of self-review with the separately tunable adversarial evaluator, and trace the engineering consequences for context allocation, compute budgeting, and audit trails.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and applied research teams building multi-step LLM pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: Separating the builder from the judge is an architectural requirement, not a prompting trick
article_ideas.thesis: The generator's failure to reject its own flawed work is a role-collision defect, not a capability deficit, so the correct fix is architectural separation of builder and judge rather than better self-critique prompting.
article_ideas.title: Verification Is Not a Prompt: Why Self-Review Fails and Split Agents Don't
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the default instinct of perpetual orchestration accretion, using the co-evolution from Sonnet 3.5 through Opus 4.6 as the case and proposing removal experiments as a standing engineering practice.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infrastructure engineers operating production agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: Harness complexity is a depreciating asset
article_ideas.thesis: Scaffolding written to compensate for model weaknesses should be versioned against model capability and deliberately removed, because a harness tuned for one model generation becomes active overhead on the next.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Harness Is a Depreciating Asset
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

article_ideas.angle: Reframe context-window lifecycle management as a first-class design decision rather than an optimization, and identify where structured handoffs beat compression.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework authors and engineers responsible for long-running workflows
article_ideas.based_on: Compaction is not a fix for long-horizon coherence loss
article_ideas.thesis: Summarization-based continuity is not a sufficient long-horizon strategy because it loses detail and causes task drift; the reliable pattern externalizes state into filesystem artifacts and treats each context window as disposable.
article_ideas.title: Compaction Is a Lie: Context Windows Should Be Disposable
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

article_ideas.angle: Show how a supposedly un-automatable evaluation dimension can be converted into a closed iteration loop, and interrogate how much of the win comes from the rubric versus from tool-using navigation.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers, AI product teams, and design-adjacent engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: Subjective qualities such as design taste and originality become machine-gradable
article_ideas.thesis: Design taste and originality become machine-gradable when decomposed into explicit rubrics and paired with a judge that actually exercises the artifact, not one that inspects it abstractly.
article_ideas.title: Grading Taste: Turning Subjective Quality into a Deterministic-Enough Loop
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

article_ideas.angle: Process/practice criticism of agent evaluation, using Zen work practice as the lens.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform and MLOps teams
article_ideas.based_on: evaluation and calibration should be woven continuously into deployed agent actions
article_ideas.thesis: Evaluation that is truly useful cannot sit apart from deployment, because an agent only becomes trustworthy by practicing every action instrumented, not by passing periodic offline tests.
article_ideas.title: The Meditation Cushion Is a Harness: Why Agent Evaluation Should Happen Inside Every Workflow

article_ideas.angle: Reliability engineering and adversarial curriculum design.
article_ideas.audience: ML researchers and reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: adversarial conditions, scarcity, and high-friction scenarios are deliberate training mechanisms
article_ideas.thesis: Agents that see only friction-free operation develop brittle confidence; hardship should be treated as intentional curriculum, not as an anomaly to exclude.
article_ideas.title: Difficulty Is a Training Signal: Designing Adversarial Scarcity for Autonomous Agents
article_ideas.video_title: The Mountain Path - 山道  (Full Documentary)

article_ideas.angle: Architecture sequencing for agent deployments.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: foundation -> guardrails -> in-the-loop practice -> unlearning/release
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomy should never precede a method layer and must include an explicit unlearning phase; the fourfold progression gives deployment a sequence that today's agent stacks mostly miss.
article_ideas.title: Foundation, Guardrails, Practice, Release: The Fourfold Path to Deployable Agents
article_ideas.video_title: The Mountain Path - 山道  (Full Documentary)

article_ideas.angle: Context hygiene in persistent agents.
article_ideas.audience: Systems engineers and LLM operations teams
article_ideas.based_on: Hermits live alone or in very small groups to minimize worldly distractions
article_ideas.thesis: Context isolation and gated interrupts are reliability features—not social constraints—because ambient noise degrades deep reasoning faster than most teams measure.
article_ideas.title: Hermit Mode: Why Long-Running Agents Need Architectural Solitude
article_ideas.video_title: The Mountain Path - 山道  (Full Documentary)

article_ideas.angle: Argue from the failure of naive truncation and summarization to the need for an explicit context architecture in agent harnesses.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and technical leaders
article_ideas.based_on: The stack is changing from prompt engineering to context engineering.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent quality is now determined by a context policy layer—what stays, what is retrieved, and what is delegated—not by prompt wording alone.
article_ideas.title: Context Engineering Is the New Full-Stack Problem
article_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

article_ideas.angle: Comparative engineering essay showing why deterministic head/tail + ID retrieval beats probabilistic summarization.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building production agents
article_ideas.based_on: LLM summarization is too inconsistent, lacks control over importance, and is unreliable.
article_ideas.thesis: LLM summarization is the wrong default for agent memory because it sacrifices control and reproducibility; an external memory store with smart truncation gives you deterministic, auditable context.
article_ideas.title: Stop Summarizing Your Agent's Memory
article_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

article_ideas.angle: Product/UX lens on context engineering, emphasizing that session continuity is a user expectation.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers and AI engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Users rarely restart chats, causing conversations and failures to appear late.
article_ideas.thesis: Long-session UX—what users remember and expect the agent to remember—should drive context retention decisions, making context management a product requirement rather than a token optimization.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Context Window Is a UX Contract
article_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

article_ideas.angle: Architectural opinion piece arguing that sub-agents are a context-budget mechanism, not just a scaling tool.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects building multi-agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: Not all context belongs in the same agent; sub-agents offload heavy tasks.
article_ideas.thesis: The real reason to delegate to sub-agents is not task decomposition but context isolation: it forces the parent to operate on distilled results, reducing bloat and cost while improving reliability.
article_ideas.title: Sub-Agents Are Your Context Budget
article_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

article_ideas.angle: A critical engineering response to AI-native SDLC marketing, foregrounding evaluation and ownership gaps
article_ideas.audience: CTOs and engineering leaders evaluating autonomous development platforms
article_ideas.based_on: 500,000 lines of code autonomously
article_ideas.thesis: 500,000 lines of agent-generated code is not proof of productivity until verification gates make that code safe to integrate; enterprises should adopt AI agents only when acceptance metrics are part of the contract.
article_ideas.title: Unverified Autonomy Is Technical Debt at Scale
article_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

article_ideas.angle: From pass@k to repo-level task metrics
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and evaluation researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Platforms with infinite code context can autonomously handle up to 80% of development sprints
article_ideas.thesis: Claims that AI platforms can own 80% of sprints with infinite context are unfalsifiable until benchmarks measure whole-repo task outcomes rather than code-completion snippets.
article_ideas.title: Infinite Context Won't Save You: The New Constraint Is Multi-File Evaluation
article_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

article_ideas.angle: Regulation as competition policy
article_ideas.audience: Policymakers, startup founders, and AI governance researchers
article_ideas.based_on: aggressive government gatekeeping or self-policing by labs will stifle competition
article_ideas.thesis: Pre-release government vetting will entrench frontier model providers unless it is built around auditable third-party red-team artifacts and compliance cost limits for small open-weight labs.
article_ideas.title: Model Vetting Is Also a Market Barrier: Designing AI Oversight Without Handing the Gate to Incumbents
article_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

article_ideas.angle: Product and monetization metrics for AI-targeted ads
article_ideas.audience: Product managers and monetization teams
article_ideas.based_on: Google search volume flattened in 2017, yet revenue continues to scale upward due to targeted AI ads
article_ideas.thesis: Search-style products should manage for incremental value per interaction generated by AI targeting rather than for queries or sessions; otherwise teams optimize the wrong thing and miss monetization.
article_ideas.title: Your Traffic Metric Is Lying to You: Google Shows AI Revenue Can Grow on Flat Search Volume
article_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

article_ideas.angle: Engineering consequence of confirmation bias in agent-generated tests and the separation-of-duties remedy.
article_ideas.audience: AI/software engineering leaders building agentic development tools
article_ideas.based_on: Tests written after implementation don't catch bugs; they confirm decisions.
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomous coding systems drift when tests are written after code; pre-committed validation contracts with adversarial, code-blind validators are required to make correctness compound over long runs.
article_ideas.title: Stop Writing Tests After Implementation: Validation Contracts for Autonomous Coding Agents
article_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Reframes the agent-building problem from raw model IQ to control-plane design and asynchronous oversight.
article_ideas.audience: AI product managers, engineering executives, and systems architects
article_ideas.based_on: The bottleneck in software engineering is not intelligence.
article_ideas.thesis: Engineering investment should shift from model capabilities to orchestration and supervision mechanisms, because the scarce resource is no longer IQ but human bandwidth to oversee many capable tasks.
article_ideas.title: The Bottleneck Is Human Attention, Not Model Intelligence
article_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Concrete scheduling rule derived from token burn and coordination overhead evidence in long-running missions.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects and distributed systems engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Coordination overhead in parallel execution can negate speed gains and burn tokens.
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent systems should default to serial execution for any task that mutates shared state; concurrency is only safe and cost-effective for conflict-free read-only operations.
article_ideas.title: Parallel Agents Are a Trap: Serialize Mutations, Parallelize Reads
article_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Communication pattern taxonomy applied to multi-agent software development; direct messages as an anti-pattern.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent systems researchers and framework developers
article_ideas.based_on: Agents DM-ing each other, hard to maintain state coherence.
article_ideas.thesis: Unmediated peer-to-peer messaging between agents makes state coherence hard; shared broadcast channels or centralized orchestrators with structured broadcasts are more robust for long-running missions.
article_ideas.title: Agent DMs Are a Coherence Nightmare: Broadcast Shared Context Instead
article_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Reframe architecture work as capability work: show how shallow-module codebases turn agent tasks into wide-context navigation problems, and argue the human's job migrates from reviewing implementations to designing boundaries.
article_ideas.audience: Senior engineers and tech leads adopting AI coding assistants inside existing codebases
article_ideas.based_on: Codebase shape becomes an input variable to agent performance
article_ideas.thesis: Refactoring toward deep modules is no longer a maintainability chore paid for by human onboarding cost; it is a direct investment in agent throughput, which means interface design quality is the binding constraint on agent reliability and the interface itself becomes the primary review surface.
article_ideas.title: Architecture Is Now an Agent Input, Not Just a Human Courtesy
article_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Name the entropy loop explicitly and specify the missing step — inspection of prior artifacts — as the fix, rather than arguing for better prompts or larger models.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers and staff engineers setting AI-assisted development policy
article_ideas.based_on: Code is not cheap; bad code is the most expensive it has ever been
article_ideas.thesis: Cheap generation does not make code cheap: the specs-to-code loop has no read/verify step, so each regeneration cycle deposits unmanaged output that degrades the very codebase the agent must work in next, making quality a throughput variable rather than a hygiene concern.
article_ideas.title: Bad Code Is the Most Expensive It Has Ever Been
article_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Turn a slogan into a scheduling rule: walk through how feedback latency sets a hard cap on step size and why easy-but-hard-to-test work is the throughput bottleneck.
article_ideas.audience: Practitioners building agent harnesses and developer-tooling engineers
article_ideas.based_on: the loop step size should be derived from time-to-feedback, not from the apparent size of the goal
article_ideas.thesis: If the rate of feedback is the system's speed limit, then step size should be derived from the latency of the cheapest verification signal rather than from the apparent logical shape of the goal, which reorganizes planning around test runtime, type checking, and browser access instead of task boundaries.
article_ideas.title: Stop Decomposing Tasks by Logic; Decompose Them by Time-to-Feedback
article_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Argue for externalized vocabularies as first-class repo citizens, then confront the drift problem the approach creates instead of treating the glossary as a one-time artifact.
article_ideas.audience: Teams practicing domain-driven design with agent-assisted implementation
article_ideas.based_on: domain context is externalized from prompts into repository artifacts
article_ideas.thesis: Treating verbosity and miscommunication as prompt defects is a category error; persisting a shared vocabulary as a versioned repo artifact makes context diffable and terminology drift observable, at the cost of a permanent synchronization obligation between glossary, code, and tests.
article_ideas.title: Move Domain Context Out of the Prompt and Into the Repository
article_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the debate from 'how good are the models' to 'what must be verifiable for this abstraction to be sound at all,' using the compiler comparison as the diagnostic rather than the reassurance.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers, platform architects, and AI infrastructure teams deciding where trust boundaries sit.
article_ideas.based_on: The abstraction argument only works when the layer below is verifiable.
article_ideas.thesis: Developers extended compiler-grade trust to LLM codegen by analogy, but compiler trust comes from deterministic translation, not from the convenience of the abstraction. Since an LLM translator is stochastic, the abstraction inherits no trust, and verification stops being a quality step and becomes the load-bearing architecture. Any team that ships an LLM step without an explicit verification layer has moved the failure surface somewhere it cannot see.
article_ideas.title: Your Abstraction Is Only as Trustworthy as the Layer You Can Verify
article_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

article_ideas.angle: Argue the inversion of source-of-truth from code to externalized theory, then show the concrete failure case where regeneration destroys uncaptured rationale.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leads, engineering managers, and teams adopting AI codegen at scale.
article_ideas.based_on: Code is not the program; the program lives inside the programmer's head.
article_ideas.thesis: If code is the shadow of the mental model, then AI generation produces shadows on demand and the durable asset is the theory — how the pieces connect and why. Teams that never externalize that theory lose it the moment they regenerate code, which makes spec and design capture the primary engineering work and makes regeneration safe only when the theory lives outside a developer's head. The practical consequence is that a repository's most valuable files are no longer its source.
article_ideas.title: Specs Are the Program Now; Your Source Code Is Disposable
article_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

article_ideas.angle: Turn the audit findings into a generation-time checklist and argue that post-hoc observability is architecturally cheaper to specify than to retrofit.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers auditing or inheriting AI-generated codebases, and founders shipping AI-built products.
article_ideas.based_on: Logs were empty, rate limiting was absent, and every failure mode was a systems thinking failure.
article_ideas.thesis: Audited AI-built applications fail in a repeating shape: monolithic files, no behavioral tests, no rate limiting, empty logs. These are not coding errors, they are omissions the generator makes by default because reliability and observability were never stated as first-class requirements. The remedy is generation-time specification of state ownership, feedback points, and error handling — patched afterward, these concerns cost more than the code they protect.
article_ideas.title: AI Codegen Always Builds the Happy Path — Reliability Has to Be Specified, Not Requested
article_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

article_ideas.angle: Connect the labor-market consequence directly to the skill argument, so the essay is about supply of judgment, not about the fate of junior developers.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, hiring managers, and educators designing developer training.
article_ideas.based_on: Junior devs lost the forcing function of writing boilerplate code by hand.
article_ideas.thesis: Automating boilerplate removed the forcing function that historically built architectural mental models, and the hiring data shows juniors contracting while senior employment rises. The skill declared essential is now the one whose supply chain was just dismantled. Organizations that treat architectural oversight as abundant will discover it is the scarcest input in the AI-first stack, and will have to manufacture it deliberately rather than hire it.
article_ideas.title: We Automated the Apprenticeship and Then Called Systems Thinking the Only Skill Left
article_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

article_ideas.angle: Control of the most dangerous failure mode AI introduces: invisible accumulation of irreversible architectural choices.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering directors and staff engineers
article_ideas.based_on: 'going solid'
article_ideas.thesis: When feature delivery no longer costs anything, it is the loss of future options that bankrupts products; engineering leaders need to track architectural plasticity as seriously as roadmap commitments.
article_ideas.title: 'Going Solid' Is the New Legacy Mess: How AI Feature Speed Turns Codebases Into Ice
article_ideas.video_title: Features vs. Futures: Software Design in the Age of AI – Kent Beck | ShipSummit | Rise8

article_ideas.angle: Interaction design of AI code generation, treated as a wish-granter not a teammate.
