deep_dives.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake
deep_dives.why: It converts rollout staging from a user-count schedule into an evaluation design problem: the criteria themselves change with scale, and a phase cannot be exited on metrics that only matter later. Without this, teams import GA-style activation metrics into a pilot that is still failing on quality.

evidence_quotes.text: Over 1,000 pull requests merged in three months on Quattro using AI-assisted review workflows.
Open source maintainers face anxiety over receiving massive floods of pull requests from AI tools.

deep_dives.research_question: What precision, false-acceptance, and defect-escape rates are achievable when maintainers replace line-by-line review with high-level AI-assisted triage and human curation?

deep_dives.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501
deep_dives.why: Open-source maintainers face a flood of generated pull requests. Quattro merged over 1,000 PRs in three months using AI-assisted review workflows, but there are no reported metrics for how often that review pipeline accepts defective code. Without such metrics, high throughput may hide scaled defects.

evidence_quotes.text: analyzes agentic patterns like 'brains and hands'

deep_dives.research_question: Under what task conditions do brains-and-hands agent structures running across multiple machines outperform a single-agent system in wall-clock time, output quality, and rollback cost?
deep_dives.topic: Distribution and Coordination Architectures for Agentic Engineering

deep_dives.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501
deep_dives.why: The interesting design space is the agent harness—separation of reasoning from execution, coordination, and transport across machines—rather than the model API. Practitioners need evidence about which decompositions are actually worthwhile.

evidence_quotes.text: Platforms have three distinct layers matching software delivery, platform lifecycle, and infrastructure
Each team must own their flow of value

deep_dives.research_question: At what organizational scale and with which platform lifecycle practices do the boundaries between Application Choreography, Platform Orchestration, and Infrastructure Orchestration become ambiguous or counterproductive?
deep_dives.topic: Where the three-tier platform model starts to break down

evidence_quotes.text: Perception is limited, meaning we are always uncertain about the state of the real world.

open_questions.why_unresolved: The claim is an executive-reported organizational metric without disclosed baseline, controls, or causal attribution.

open_questions.question: Which layer is load-bearing in Salesforce's architecture: the unified platform rewrite, Data Cloud unification, or the Agentforce reasoning layer?
open_questions.research_direction: Benchmark agent reliability and resolution rates against varying levels of data integration and platform consolidation across multiple enterprise deployments.
open_questions.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141
open_questions.why_unresolved: Salesforce adopted all three simultaneously, so the summary does not compare alternative architectures or isolate the causal contribution of each component.

open_questions.question: After achieving ~95% autonomous resolution, what is the optimal digital-agent-to-human-agent ratio for support operations in terms of cost, quality, and customer satisfaction?
open_questions.research_direction: Model escalation cost, CSAT, regulatory risk, and human availability as functions of automation depth to identify optimal fallback thresholds.
open_questions.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary asserts headcount reduction and rebalancing but provides no optimization criteria or measurement of quality impact.

open_questions.question: What are the local interaction rules driving the behaviour of our agentic system, and which of them can produce uncontrolled emergent global effects?
open_questions.research_direction: Systematically map agent interaction rules (when to call tools, how context is shared, how retries are triggered) and run parameter sweeps in agent-based models to find phase boundaries.
open_questions.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
open_questions.why_unresolved: The video shows that macro outcomes cannot be reliably deduced from micro-level preferences or rules; you need simulation or observation to discover which local rules amplify.

open_questions.question: Are we mistaking a complex system for a Newtonian machine?
open_questions.research_direction: Design perturbation experiments: change one interaction parameter slightly and measure whether outcomes scale continuously or jump discontinuously; if jumps appear, treat the system as complex rather than machine-like.
open_questions.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
open_questions.why_unresolved: Newtonian thinking assumes predictability, rationality, measurability, and control, but complex systems with interactions and feedback violate those assumptions in ways that are hard to see from inside the system.

open_questions.question: Where are the hidden positive feedback loops in a production multi-agent system, and can their strength be monitored online?
open_questions.research_direction: Instrument rate-of-change and correlation of signals across agents; test early-warning indicators such as rising variance, slowing recovery, or critical slowing down before collapse.
open_questions.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
open_questions.why_unresolved: Positive feedback loops are not visible as static metrics; they are self-reinforcing rates such as retry amplification, context contamination, or tool-use concentration that can push a system over a tipping point.

open_questions.question: Do power-law failure distributions actually appear in real agent-system incidents, and how heavy are the tails?
open_questions.research_direction: Collect incident sizes and frequencies across agent workloads; fit distributions on log-log axes and compare power-law against lognormal/exponential alternatives to plan capacity and risk.
open_questions.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
open_questions.why_unresolved: The video documents power laws in natural and social systems, but the summary provides no direct evidence of heavy tails in engineered multi-agent systems.

open_questions.question: Can complex global coordination in agentic systems be achieved with only a small set of local rules, or is central orchestration still necessary for task-level accountability?
open_questions.research_direction: Benchmark decentralized local-rule agents against centralized orchestrators on tasks requiring coordination, resilience, and accountability, varying the number and abstraction of local rules.
open_questions.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
open_questions.why_unresolved: The starling flock example shows complex patterns emerging from three local rules, but the summary does not specify when such decentralization is sufficient for goal-directed agentic tasks.

open_questions.question: How can an agent system automatically infer the polarity of feedback loops from its own action and observation traces?
open_questions.research_direction: Use causal discovery or LLM-generated causal graphs over logged actions and state changes to classify loops as reinforcing or balancing.
open_questions.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
open_questions.why_unresolved: Loop polarity is currently a manual causal diagramming exercise; traces contain correlation, not causal structure.

open_questions.question: How should context and memory be designed as stocks with explicit inflow and outflow policies in long-running agents?
open_questions.research_direction: Prototype memory managers that expose inflow/outflow controls and benchmark summarization/eviction policies against task performance.
open_questions.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
open_questions.why_unresolved: Stocks and flows are an abstract modeling concept; there is no standard API for memory inflow (write) and outflow (forget/summarize) rates.

open_questions.question: How can an agent measure the delay between its own actions and observable environmental effects?
open_questions.research_direction: Add delay tracking metadata to tool calls and learn per-environment delay distributions; then test dampening or wait-for-effect policies.
open_questions.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
open_questions.why_unresolved: Delays are usually not instrumented in agent harnesses, and environment causality is noisy.

open_questions.question: Can an agent's internal 'mental model' be elicited and corrected to avoid policy resistance?
open_questions.research_direction: Require agents to state assumptions and expected effects before acting, then compare against observed outcomes to detect model drift.
open_questions.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
open_questions.why_unresolved: Mental models are internal and not directly observable, making it hard to identify when they filter important feedback.

open_questions.question: What does an operationalized boundary-judgement process look like for an agentic system: who chooses the context/knowledge/tool boundary, how is it contested, and how often is it revisited?
open_questions.research_direction: Design explicit boundary-setting interfaces, log boundary decisions as metadata, and experimentally compare fixed vs. revisable context scopes.
open_questions.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
open_questions.why_unresolved: The source only establishes that boundary lines are subjective judgements, not objective features, so there is no algorithmic mechanism supplied for making the choice.

open_questions.question: Can VSM be used as a diagnostic audit for existing agentic architectures, and does the absence of any of the five functions correlate with observed failure modes in production?
open_questions.research_direction: Map deployed agent systems onto VSM, identify missing functions, and prospectively test whether adding, say, an explicit environment-scanning loop improves long-horizon task reliability.
open_questions.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
open_questions.why_unresolved: VSM evidence in the source comes from modeling organizations and public-sector services, not from generative-agent deployments.

open_questions.question: Which metrics capture systemic properties of agent systems so they can be tracked across changes?
open_questions.research_direction: Create canonical multi-agent scenario benchmarks with whole-system outcomes (e.g., robustness to perturbation, coordination efficiency, intent preservation) and study their sensitivity to individual component changes.
open_questions.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
open_questions.why_unresolved: The source contrasts component-level reductionism with whole-level systemic properties but does not define operational system-level metrics.

open_questions.question: Which PSMs can be translated into agent workflows, and what is the human-AI division of labor when running them?
open_questions.research_direction: Prototype an agent that elicits a rich picture from stakeholders and compares output quality and participant learning against traditional facilitated workshops.
open_questions.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary describes rich pictures and workshops as social facilitation techniques but says nothing about automating them through AI agents.

open_questions.question: Which parts of a claimed internal-state capability are externally measurable, and do those measurements predict downstream behavioral capability?
open_questions.research_direction: Run controlled instrumented trials of a single claimed effect and test whether the measured signal correlates with any externally scored capability.

open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary asserts one measurable effect ('measurable body heat in freezing conditions') and leaves the rest as named but unmeasured substrates (wind channels, prana, nadi, bindu).

open_questions.question: Which knowledge actually survives an institutional wipeout: stored artifacts, or procedures embodied in distributed operators?
open_questions.research_direction: Compare recovery outcomes under artifact-loss-only versus operator-loss-only conditions in a controlled replication study.
open_questions.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary reports both massive destruction of texts and libraries and the survival of the tradition through new centers, without isolating which carrier was decisive.

open_questions.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary states the advanced modules require retreat conditions and a qualified teacher but gives no data on whether the gate is load-bearing or merely conventional.

open_questions.question: Does periodic re-assertion of a small invariant instruction set actually suppress drift in long-running agents, and what does it cost in flexibility?
open_questions.research_direction: Instrument long agent runs with and without scheduled re-anchoring and measure drift, task success, and adaptation loss.
open_questions.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film
open_questions.why_unresolved: The reining-in mechanism is asserted as a practice ('repetition of core beliefs, mantras, and meditation') with no measurement of effect size or side effects.

project_ideas.based_on: Created an unmonitored communication channel to bypass sandbox containment
project_ideas.hypothesis: An egress proxy that records hashes and topic signatures of every public write made by an agent can detect when two nominally isolated agents use a public wiki as a shared blackboard with an F1 score of at least 0.90, while still allowing ordinary web operations.
project_ideas.measurement: ROC AUC and F1 of covert-channel detection over 1,000 runs; false-positive rate on legitimate wiki edits; time-to-detection after the first cross-write.
project_ideas.name: Egress Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a testbed where two agents are firewalled from each other but both may read and write an obscure wiki; make one agent encode task hints in posts and the other retrieve them, then compare audit logs plus proxy scores against a no-coordination baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: 10,000 agents, 130 billion tokens, and 88 hours of compute produced a claimed solution to a Millennium problem
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a benchmark of 100 Olympiad-level and graduate-level math problems, a 50-agent fan-out with explicit task decomposition, checkpointing, and an independent proof checker will solve at least 20% more problems than a single-agent best-of-100 sampler at the same total token budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Verified solve rate per 100M tokens, lemma checkpoint success rate, and false-positive rate before verification.
project_ideas.name: FleetProver
project_ideas.poc: Build a durable task queue in which an orchestrator splits a theorem into lemmas, worker agents produce candidate proofs, failed branches resume from checkpoints, and an independent verifier aggregates only checked results; compare against repeated single-agent sampling.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: Generation model, Autorater / Critique, Prompt rewriting, Optimizer agent
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an autorater and prompt-rewriting pass will improve human-acceptance rate of generated API documentation and README files by at least 30% after two revisions compared with one-shot generation, at no more than 2.5x the inference cost per accepted artifact.
project_ideas.measurement: Acceptance rate by revision, inference cost per accepted artifact, and critic-human agreement on failure reasons.
project_ideas.name: CriticLoop
project_ideas.poc: Create a fixed task set of 200 documentation-generation prompts; run a generator-critic-rewriter loop for up to five revisions; validate acceptance with a held-out LLM judge and a small human-rater sample.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: GPT-6 Astra recreated Manhattan street-by-street from a simple text prompt in one week
project_ideas.hypothesis: If a text-prompt world generator can create a city-like environment, then specifying scenario parameters such as traffic density, obstacles, and time pressure will monotonically shift agent success rates across 50 seeded world instances, enabling calibrated difficulty without hand-built fixtures.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between specified difficulty and mean solve rate; within-seed variance; reproducibility under identical world seed.
project_ideas.name: WorldBench
project_ideas.poc: Connect a generated city world API to an agent harness; generate 50 environment seeds at low, medium, and high specified difficulty; run a fixed agent population while recording per-seed traces and event logs.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: Handles tool call notifications and permission requests.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A client-side ACP middleware can intercept every permission request from any compliant harness and return allow/deny responses via a uniform policy and audit store, with no harness-specific code and 100% capture.
project_ideas.measurement: Proportion of permission requests captured per harness, decision-log schema consistency across harnesses, and end-to-end approval latency.
project_ideas.name: ACP Consent Gate
project_ideas.poc: Build a middleware that reads ACP tool-call notifications and permission-request messages, presents a generic user prompt, and returns permission responses; then run two different ACP-compatible harnesses through identical tool-call prompts.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: Having the same protocol semantics over stdio, HTTP, and WebSocket makes agent execution location a deployment detail
project_ideas.hypothesis: A single ACP client can drive the same stdio-connected harness remotely by swapping only the transport layer; local and remote runs will show the same JSON-RPC method types and ordering and comparable task success rates.
project_ideas.measurement: JSON-RPC method-name and ordering match ratio between local and remote sessions over 20 runs, task success rate, and median latency overhead.
project_ideas.name: ACP Remote Execution Bridge
project_ideas.poc: Implement a bridge process that exposes an ACP harness over HTTP/WebSocket and forwards to a child stdio harness; run a fixed task against a local connection and against the bridge while capturing all JSON-RPC traffic.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: How do ACP clients and harnesses negotiate capabilities at session establishment?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A session-level conformance corpus will detect cross-client/cross-harness capability-negotiation mismatches that single-implementation tests miss; running N clients against N harnesses will yield reproducible mismatch categories.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-product pass/fail counts, mismatch categories, and number of methods not supported or improperly negotiated.
project_ideas.name: ACP Interop Matrix
project_ideas.poc: Encode ACP sessions covering session creation, user messages, tool-call notifications, permission responses, and capability negotiation as versioned YAML scenarios; run every client-harness pair and record protocol-level failures.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: custom methods prefixed with underscores
project_ideas.hypothesis: Underscore-prefixed extension usage is either highly concentrated in a few shared methods, indicating convergence, or long-tailed, indicating fragmentation, and this pattern can be measured from observable JSON-RPC traffic.
project_ideas.measurement: Share of underscore method calls, top-five method concentration ratio, and number of implementations per custom method.
project_ideas.name: ACP Extension Landscape Analyzer
project_ideas.poc: Collect JSON-RPC method usage logs from a small set of ACP clients and harnesses; classify standard methods versus underscore-prefixed extension methods; cluster method names by implementation.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: Runs the entire system in a hostile simulation with targeted and fuzz testing
project_ideas.hypothesis: A CI gate that runs the full agent system inside a deliberately hostile simulated environment with targeted and fuzz testing, and that fails builds only with full reproduction steps attached, catches a strictly larger set of real defects per engineer-hour than human line-level review of the same changes.
project_ideas.measurement: Defects escaped to production per 100 merged changes; median time from failure to confirmed reproduction; review hours displaced per defect caught.
project_ideas.name: Hostile Harness Gate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agentic codebase with a simulation driver that injects hostile conditions, run targeted plus fuzz suites in CI, and force every failure artifact to carry an executable reproduction. Run in parallel with standard human review for one quarter and compare defect escape rates and time-to-triage.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: Bridging local execution tools with cloud infrastructure requires careful architectural alignment
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent runtime whose tool and state interfaces are defined as boundary-agnostic will migrate from local execution to a managed cloud stack with no rewrite of the execution loop, whereas a runtime that assumes local filesystem and implicit trust will require one.
project_ideas.measurement: Lines changed in the execution loop during migration; state-consistency violations under concurrent local and remote execution; added tool-call latency.
project_ideas.name: Boundary-Agnostic Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Implement one minimal tool-calling agent twice: (a) with filesystem, process and credentials abstracted behind a portable interface, and (b) with direct local assumptions. Then move both behind a remote sandbox and measure the diff surface of the execution loop.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: Rust proved to be very good for agents fairly quickly when effort was put into it
project_ideas.hypothesis: Given identical tool semantics and identical model calls, a Rust agent harness exhibits a lower rate of unrecovered runtime failures and lower tail latency under injected tool-call faults than an equivalent harness in a garbage-collected language.
project_ideas.measurement: Unrecovered failure rate per 1,000 tool calls; p99 latency under fault injection; recovery success rate; development effort to reach parity.
project_ideas.name: Harness Language Fault Study
project_ideas.poc: Build the same minimal tool-calling loop in Rust and in one GC'd language with a shared tool schema and fault-injection driver. Subject both to identical tool-call faults — timeouts, malformed responses, partial writes — and compare failure and recovery behavior.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: Focus on co-designing models and harnesses together
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scores produced by an evaluation harness that rates model and harness configurations jointly will rank configurations differently than scores from a fixed stable model API, and the divergence will be large enough to change at least one shipping decision.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between joint scores and fixed-contract scores; per-task score delta attributable to harness-specific formatting; number of shipping decisions the divergence would reverse.
project_ideas.name: Joint Model-Harness Scoring Bench
project_ideas.poc: Define a joint scoring harness over a fixed task set, evaluate the same model under a stable API contract versus a harness-specific context format and tool schema, and compare rankings and per-task deltas.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: How can silent forgetting be detected in production without ground truth?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A separate per-constraint verifier pass can attribute which specific rules of a long skills file were violated by an already-generated completion, achieving materially higher per-rule detection of silent forgetting than a single holistic LLM-as-judge score.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-rule precision/recall against a synthetic ground truth where the exact dropped rules are known by construction, compared head-to-head with a single holistic judge score on the same outputs.
project_ideas.name: Rule Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Build a self-audit stage that takes a completed agent output plus the N-rule skills file and returns a per-rule followed/violated/unverifiable verdict, then run it on IFScale-style outputs from a model known to fail silently past its threshold.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: IFScale-style evaluation is a portable harness pattern
project_ideas.hypothesis: Running a fixed density-accuracy harness across model versions locates each model's instruction cliff within a narrow band, and the cliff position for tool-selection and format constraints differs from the keyword-count cliff by more than the run-to-run variance.
project_ideas.measurement: Constraint count at which accuracy drops below a fixed threshold, with confidence intervals across repeated runs, compared per constraint class and per model.
project_ideas.name: Cliff Finder
project_ideas.poc: Port the IFScale-style report generation harness to two agentic constraint classes (tool-selection policy and output-format invariants), sweep constraint density on a log scale, and plot accuracy against N for each model and class.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: Safety classifiers evaluate aggregate context and can fire on sparse lexical triggers embedded in large instruction sets
project_ideas.hypothesis: False-positive refusal rate on benign context grows monotonically with the number of constraints and ingested tokens, and a lightweight pre-flight scan plus reroute recovers most of the resulting lost completions at negligible quality cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Refusal rate versus constraint density curve, and recovery rate plus quality delta when the reroute path is enabled.
project_ideas.name: Refusal Thermometer
project_ideas.poc: Inject benign-but-triggering tokens into otherwise identical skills files at varying constraint counts, measure refusal rate as a function of density, then test a pre-flight trigger scan plus model reroute against the baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: Reasoning budget is a finite, shared resource that can be consumed without producing output
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tracking reasoning tokens separately from output tokens and aborting or forcing a fallback when reasoning consumes more than a set fraction of the total budget materially reduces zero-result completions without degrading task quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of completions with no usable result, plus task-quality score, in guarded versus unguarded runs at identical total token budgets.
project_ideas.name: Budget Split Alarm
project_ideas.poc: Wrap agent calls with dual-budget accounting and a no-result detector that fires when the completion contains no deliverable payload, then compare abort-and-retry routing against the unguarded baseline on hard multi-constraint tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: conflict resolution as a distinct subsystem, not as prompt instructions
project_ideas.hypothesis: A hybrid resolution policy combining source authority with recency weighting yields higher agent answer accuracy on contradictory multi-source context than either recency-only or human-adjudication-last policies.
project_ideas.measurement: Answer accuracy and contradiction-detection rate per policy, plus the fraction of conflicts a policy leaves unresolved or resolves wrongly.
project_ideas.name: ConflictBench
project_ideas.poc: Generate synthetic conflicts across code, docs, Slack, and incident records (old architecture record versus last night's Slack thread) and route each through three pluggable resolution policies, scoring agent answers against a ground-truth winning source.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: satisfaction of search bias
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pre-ranked, engine-side context payloads reduce premature-retrieval-termination rate and total search loops versus an agent driving raw MCP search tools directly.
project_ideas.measurement: Premature-termination rate, retrieval-call count per task, and token spend per task in each configuration.
project_ideas.name: StopOrGo
project_ideas.poc: Run a fixed task set in two configurations — agent-with-MCP-search versus agent-over-hydrated-engine-payload — instrumenting how many retrieval calls occur before the agent answers and whether the authoritative source was ever read.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: silent failures where code compiles but breaks production
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents run without institutional context violate unstated feature-flag and rollout requirements at a materially higher rate than hydrated agents, even when both produce compiling code.
project_ideas.measurement: Violation rate per 100 tasks, split by hydrated/unhydrated, with compile-success rate held constant to isolate silent failures.
project_ideas.name: SilentFailSuite
project_ideas.poc: Build golden tasks whose correct solution depends on a feature-flag or rollout rule that never appears in the prompt, then compare hydrated versus unhydrated agent output against the rule set rather than the compiler.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: Curated-context repos rot faster than you can update them
project_ideas.hypothesis: Hand-curated markdown context repos decay measurably faster than a maintained ingestion pipeline, but the engine incurs its own staleness and conflict rates that approach curated-repo levels without active monitoring.
project_ideas.measurement: Staleness half-life in days, contradiction discovery rate per week, and maintenance hours per source per month for each approach.
project_ideas.name: ContextRotMeter
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a curated rules repo and a context engine side by side in an active codebase, logging staleness events and source contradictions over time against a fixed fact set.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: How do RLM overhead costs compare across different base models in production?
project_ideas.hypothesis: RLM overhead cost (tokens, latency, dollars) scales superlinearly with recursion depth and inversely with base-model coding ability, making the architecture uneconomical below a certain capability tier.
project_ideas.measurement: Dollars per completed task and p95 latency vs. base-model coding benchmark score and recursion depth.
project_ideas.name: RLM Cost Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an RLM harness to log token usage, wall-clock time, and sub-call count per recursion level; run on a fixed long-horizon task across 3–5 base models of varying coding ability; fit a cost model.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: At what point does recursive decomposition stop helping relative to the reported ~40% context-usage degradation threshold?
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a measurable input-size and context-utilization threshold above which an RLM harness outperforms a RAG baseline on long-horizon reasoning, after normalizing for latency and dollar cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy delta and cost per correct answer as a function of input size and context utilization.
project_ideas.name: RLM Crossover Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal RLM harness (REPL + sub-LM calls) and a RAG baseline on a long-document QA task; sweep input sizes and context utilization levels; measure accuracy, latency, and cost per task.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: What are the best practices for structuring sub-LM signatures in DSPy?
project_ideas.hypothesis: The granularity and typing of sub-LM signatures in a DSPy-based RLM significantly affects recursion depth and final accuracy; overly coarse signatures increase context per sub-call while overly fine ones explode call count.
project_ideas.measurement: ROUGE/BERTScore vs. recursion depth and call count.
project_ideas.name: Sub-LM Signature Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Build three versions of a document-summarization RLM with different sub-LM signature granularities; evaluate on summarization quality, recursion depth, and total calls.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: The RLM pattern separates a deterministic execution shell (REPL) from a probabilistic core (LLM)
project_ideas.hypothesis: A deterministic REPL shell that traces executed code, serializes state, and supports replay reduces debugging time and failure recurrence in recursive agents compared to unstructured tool-calling.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean time to diagnosis (MTTD) and failure recurrence rate.
project_ideas.name: Deterministic Shell Observability
project_ideas.poc: Add tracing and replay to an RLM harness; run a failure-prone task; measure time-to-diagnose and failure recurrence with and without the shell.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: the breakthrough was achieving human-like emotional intonation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Standard auto-MOS/WER metrics cannot detect loss of emotional prosody; an 'emotion intent' listener test will rank TTS models differently on expressive material.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman rank correlation between standard quality scores and emotional-fidelity ratings; responder agreement (Fleiss' kappa) on emotional failure.
project_ideas.name: prosody-gap TTS evaluation harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a small set of utterances with marked emotional intent (e.g., grief, joy, urgency) in multiple languages; run several TTS models; produce audio clips; collect listener ratings on whether the emotion came through; compare to standard metric scores.
project_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

project_ideas.based_on: Marketplace models allow creators and individuals to authenticate, share, and monetize their AI voices
project_ideas.hypothesis: Synthetic voice generation can be gated by a signed consent artifact for the target voice with lower than 100ms added latency, making identity checks practical at API scale.
project_ideas.measurement: Added latency P99; invalid-token rejection rate; valid-token acceptance rate; watermark traceability in generated files.
project_ideas.name: voice-consent ledger sidecar
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a TTS endpoint with a consent-checking proxy; issue signed consent tokens for voice profiles; proxy rejects requests without a valid token and tags generations with a watermark or request ID; measure overhead.
project_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

project_ideas.based_on: Customer obsession as a form of R&D
project_ideas.hypothesis: Support conversations about a deployed speech product can be automatically classified into model capability gaps (robotic tone, mispronunciation, lack of emotion) and the resulting gap ranking predicts the model improvements shipped in the next release cycle better than raw feature-request counts.
project_ideas.measurement: F1 for capability-gap classification; overlap and rank correlation between gap list and actual shipped capabilities.
project_ideas.name: capability-gap classifier for AI product roadmaps
project_ideas.poc: Anonymize and label support tickets/customer logs from speech API; use an LLM to tag failure modes; produce a ranked gap list; compare with release notes/changelog over two subsequent quarters.
project_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

project_ideas.based_on: AI is exceptional at seeing weak signals and synthesizing competitive advantage data
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM weak-signal synthesis precision, recall, and calibration can be measured against expert human analyst conclusions on a multi-source corpus, and LLMs will show systematic overconfidence in low-signal conditions.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, calibration error (ECE), and overconfidence frequency compared to expert baseline.
project_ideas.name: WeakSignalBench
project_ideas.poc: Curate 50 company corpora, have experts label advantage drivers and disruption threats, run an LLM agent to synthesize conclusions, and compare AI outputs to expert labels.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: AI should be evaluated along three distinct vectors
project_ideas.hypothesis: A system can score high on productivity metrics while remaining neutral or negative on structural (disintermediation) metrics, and separate instrumentation reveals this divergence.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-vector scores and the magnitude of divergence between productivity and structural vectors.
project_ideas.name: ThreeVectorDash
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an AI workflow with per-vector metrics: productivity (time/cost), innovation (profit-pool impact), structural (value-chain boundary shifts). Run on multiple case studies and compare scores.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: Anchoring to a prior baseline ('last year's budget') is identified as a primary trap
project_ideas.hypothesis: An allocation policy that re-derives resource (compute, context, tools) from strategic targets on a cadence, while retaining a frozen reference baseline for regression detection, increases reallocation intensity without losing regression detection.
project_ideas.measurement: Reallocation magnitude, task performance, and regression detection rate.
project_ideas.name: ReallocAgent
project_ideas.poc: Simulate an agent tuning loop with two policies: anchored to previous baseline vs target-derived. Compare reallocation magnitude, task performance, and regression detection over multiple iterations.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: Mobilization is only effective when institutionalized
project_ideas.hypothesis: There is a minimum enforcement strength in a harness (advisory vs. mandatory reallocation) below which alignment degrades under personnel/context turnover; above which it persists.
project_ideas.measurement: Alignment persistence score under turnover and reallocation adherence rate.
project_ideas.name: DefaultAlignHarness
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness with configurable enforcement for resource reallocation. Simulate turnover cycles (changing agents, contexts) and measure alignment persistence over time.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: The hard part is not finding the right answer, it is asking the right question.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A question-ranking model trained to maximize expected reduction in solution-space branching will select the expert-judged eigenquestion at least 70% more often than a baseline that asks for generic clarification.
project_ideas.measurement: Top-1 match with expert ranking; improvement in downstream task success when the agent asks the top predicted question before planning, versus baseline question order.
project_ideas.name: Question Value Probe: Ranking Clarifying Questions as Eigenquestions
project_ideas.poc: On an existing set of underspecified coding/planning tasks, enumerate candidate questions, generate possible solution plans for each candidate, compute average pairwise plan edit distance as a proxy for solution-space reduction, and compare predicted top question to human-annotated eigenquestion.
project_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

project_ideas.based_on: Superhuman Go providing inline assistance and triggers without requiring users to prompt manually.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An event-triggered agent that only sees the current buffer/document and surfaces one inline suggestion will reduce the number of user actions required to complete a document-editing workflow by at least 40% compared with a chat agent that requires context pasting, with no increase in user-corrected edits.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of user actions and prompts, accepted vs user-corrected suggestion rate, user-reported confidence in 10 participants.
project_ideas.name: Tightrope: Permissioned Assist Agent in a Live Editor
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal VS Code extension or browser email client plugin that fires on save/typing/compose events within a single document scope, runs a knowledge-check prompt, and shows accept/reject inline diffs; run the same task via chat-only baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

project_ideas.based_on: MongoDB Atlas serves as a data layer for AI apps and agents without needing completely new stacks.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a realistic email/document agent workload, a single operational DB with vector search can match a purpose-built vector DB within 5 percentage points of recall@10 and within 2x p95 latency, with atomic state updates and a simpler ops footprint.
project_ideas.measurement: recall@10, p95/p99 latency, throughput under simultaneous writes, operational complexity in number of services and sync jobs.
project_ideas.name: One-Store Agent: Unified Operational + Vector Store Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Take a snapshot of documents/emails and generate embeddings; replay hybrid queries where filters restrict on source/status and distance scores rank semantically against a purpose-built vector database running the same embeddings; concurrently write state updates to both stores.
project_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

project_ideas.based_on: Grammarly generating over 100 billion LLM queries a week at thousands per user daily.
project_ideas.hypothesis: If an assist agent triggers only on events for which an inexpensive local model predicts high suggestion acceptance probability, it can match all-event triggering in accepted suggestions per user session while reducing daily LLM calls and cost by more than 50%.
project_ideas.measurement: Accepted suggestions per session, dismissed/undo rate, LLM calls per user per day, user opt-out rate.
project_ideas.name: Trigger Budget: Utility-Gated Proactive Assist
project_ideas.poc: Extend the Tightrope assist-mode prototype with a trigger gating classifier using local features such as event type, text diff size, recency, and document metadata; compare all-event triggers vs gated triggers over the same user workflow tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

project_ideas.based_on: Prefix caching allows sharing prompts across users and sessions, saving prefill compute in repeated agent/chat workloads.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a vLLM-served agent test harness, keeping the system prompt and tool schema byte-identical at the beginning of every turn yields >60% prefix-cache hit rate and at least 25% lower p50 prefill time than the same workload when a timestamp or random user ID is injected before the stable prefix.
project_ideas.measurement: Prefix-cache hit ratio and prefill time (p50/p95) for each prompt variant.
project_ideas.name: prefix-cache-diagnostic
project_ideas.poc: Replay a corpus of multi-turn agent traces through vLLM using two prompt variants (cache-friendly stable prefix vs variable prefix), record cache hit rates and prefill TTFT via vLLM metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher

project_ideas.based_on: Quantizing Mistral-7B from FP16 to INT4 reduces weight memory from 14.5 GB to 3.6 GB.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Running a representative 7B-8B model in INT4/NF4 on a vLLM server decreases success on a multi-step tool-use benchmark by at least 10 percentage points compared to FP16, even when perplexity deltas are small.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end task success rate and error category distribution for FP16 vs INT4.
project_ideas.name: int4-agent-reliability-check
project_ideas.poc: Create an executable tool-calling task set; run the same agent harness with FP16 and INT4/NF4 weights under identical prompts and sampling temperature; compare success, parse-error, and retry-frequency rates.
project_ideas.video_title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher

project_ideas.based_on: Mistral-7B decode step streams 14.5 GB from HBM to SRAM on every step.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding output length constant on an A100-class GPU, increasing the input context length by 2x increases measured per-token decode latency by at least 10% because every decode step scans the KV cache from HBM.
project_ideas.measurement: Inter-token latency (ITL) and achieved HBM bandwidth as a function of context length.
project_ideas.name: decode-bandwidth-probe
project_ideas.poc: Use vLLM to issue constant-output-length generation requests with varying context lengths; profile with GPU hardware counters and log token-level latencies; compare observed bytes-per-step to the roofline prediction.
project_ideas.video_title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher

project_ideas.based_on: The architectural boundary that matters is where the agent executes
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tasks requiring background execution and multi-step state achieve significantly higher end-to-end completion rates when the agent owns a persistent environment compared to session-based tool calling.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, time to completion, user supervision time, and recovery success after failures.
project_ideas.name: Agent Substrate Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a suite of 20 knowledge-work tasks (e.g., drafting and sending email sequences, scheduling with follow-up, research synthesis) and execute them under two architectures: (a) agent as a chat session invoking tools, (b) agent as a bot with its own VM and persistent filesystem. Recruit 10 users to supervise both.
project_ideas.video_title: How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte (SpaceXAI)

project_ideas.based_on: Natural language is used as the automation primitive, deliberately replacing traditional trigger/workflow builders
project_ideas.hypothesis: Compiling natural-language automation instructions into inspectable, editable specs improves reliability and debuggability without reducing adoption by non-technical users.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate of scheduled executions, time to debug a failed automation, user satisfaction (SUS), and number of edits to compiled specs.
project_ideas.name: NL Automation Compiler
project_ideas.poc: Implement a system that takes plain-English recurring/conditional tasks (e.g., 'remind me at 8 AM daily') and produces a structured schedule that can be viewed, edited, and version-controlled. Test with 15 non-technical users over two weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte (SpaceXAI)

project_ideas.based_on: What authorization and isolation model lets a bot hold long-lived credentials for company tools while remaining auditable and revocable?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-bot scoped credentials with mandatory action logs preserve agent autonomy while reducing the blast radius of a compromised agent compared to shared service accounts.
project_ideas.measurement: Scope of unauthorized access, time to revoke credentials, audit log completeness, and task success rate under normal operation.
project_ideas.name: Agent Credential Isolation Prototype
project_ideas.poc: Create a bot with its own identity and scoped tokens for three company tools (e.g., email, calendar, CRM). Simulate a compromised agent (prompt injection) and measure containment. Compare with a bot using a shared admin account.
project_ideas.video_title: How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte (SpaceXAI)

project_ideas.based_on: The team manually onboarded 200-300 users in high-touch sessions
project_ideas.hypothesis: A structured manual onboarding protocol for 20 users yields a failure taxonomy and use-case distribution that automated telemetry misses in the first month of an agent product.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of unique failure modes discovered, number of product decisions changed, and overlap between manual and telemetry findings.
project_ideas.name: Manual Onboarding as Evaluation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Conduct 20 one-hour manual onboarding sessions with target users, logging every failure, confusion, and workaround. Simultaneously collect automated telemetry from the same sessions. Compare the sets of issues discovered.
project_ideas.video_title: How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte (SpaceXAI)

project_ideas.based_on: Epiplexity measures the structural information a *computationally bounded* observer can extract from data
project_ideas.hypothesis: Selecting training data by epiplexity (time-bounded MDL) yields better out-of-distribution generalization than dedup or perplexity filtering at the same compute budget.
project_ideas.measurement: OOD accuracy and achieved compression (bits per token) versus baseline curation methods.
project_ideas.name: Epiplexity-Guided Data Curation
project_ideas.poc: Implement a tractable epiplexity estimator during training; use it to curate subsets of a text/code corpus; train a small model on each subset and compare OOD transfer.
project_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

project_ideas.based_on: Generalization is achieved not by restricting model capacity but by pairing an expressive hypothesis space with a *soft* preference for compressible solutions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Increasing model capacity while adding a soft compression penalty (e.g., MDL regularization) shrinks the generalization gap more than capacity increase alone at equal data and compute.
project_ideas.measurement: Generalization gap (test minus train loss) as a function of model size, with and without soft bias.
project_ideas.name: Soft Bias Scaling Law
project_ideas.poc: Train models of varying parameter counts with and without a soft compression bias; measure held-out generalization gap and achieved compression.
project_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

project_ideas.based_on: Sequence direction / factorization order matters empirically even though classical information theory treats information as independent of factorization order
project_ideas.hypothesis: The order in which tool outputs and reasoning steps are serialized into an agent trajectory significantly affects downstream task success and learnability.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate and sample efficiency (steps to converge) across orderings.
project_ideas.name: Trajectory Ordering Optimization
project_ideas.poc: Generate agent trajectories with different orderings (e.g., tool calls before vs. after reasoning, context placement) and evaluate task success and training efficiency when fine-tuning on each ordering.
project_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

project_ideas.based_on: The first information paradox: classical theory says deterministic processes cannot create information (data processing inequality), yet synthetic data generation and pseudorandom generators enable superhuman systems like AlphaZero
project_ideas.hypothesis: Self-play with bounded compute can produce novel extractable structure (strategies, compressed representations) not present in the seed data, contradicting the data processing inequality intuition.
project_ideas.measurement: Performance beyond seed data, and information-theoretic novelty of generated trajectories relative to seed.
project_ideas.name: Self-Play Structure Emergence
project_ideas.poc: Run self-play in a game (e.g., AlphaZero-style) and measure new strategies or compressed representations that outperform the seed data's best.
project_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

project_ideas.based_on: Adding a meta-harness to Claude Code on Terminal Bench 2 gave an 18% accuracy bump.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Re-running a fixed base agent with a versioned meta-harness on Terminal Bench 2 will reproduce an accuracy improvement large enough that harness version matters more than a typical point-model update.
project_ideas.measurement: Terminal Bench 2 task success rates for each harness variant, with bootstrapped confidence intervals and per-task error deltas.
project_ideas.name: HarnessAttribute
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark runner that pins one base agent and toggles only the meta-harness layer, with per-task logs, git-pinned harness versions, and a no-meta-harness control.
project_ideas.video_title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club

project_ideas.based_on: L2 REPL and Subagents (Agentic Garbage Collection)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Explicit L2 agentic garbage collection via subagent summarization keeps active context token count bounded and preserves or improves task success compared with a no-op context manager on long-horizon coding tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Context token counts at predefined task milestones, task completion rate, total token cost, and wall-clock time.
project_ideas.name: Agent Memory GC
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent runtime to log context growth, then run 20 long-horizon tasks in two modes: default context accumulation versus subagent-based compaction of stale L2 state.
project_ideas.video_title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club

project_ideas.based_on: Continual learning harnesses allow models to update prompts, tools, and system states iteratively.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A self-modifying harness that tests prompt and tool mutations offline before promotion will improve held-out task success by a meaningful margin over a fixed harness while never regressing below the fixed-harness baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Average success rate of promoted candidates, number of rollbacks, and score difference on the held-out suite against the fixed-harness control.
project_ideas.name: Harness Auto-Tuner with Rollback
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a task agent with a prompt optimizer that saves each candidate harness state, evaluates it on a held-out suite, and only promotes mutations that pass a regression threshold; keep a rollback registry for all promoted states.
project_ideas.video_title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club

project_ideas.based_on: As models get better, harnesses need to become more complicated to allow models to do more things
project_ideas.hypothesis: Given a fixed agentic task suite, a measurable subset of harness components (auto-mode classifiers, verification steps, escalation rules) becomes redundant as the underlying model improves, and ablating those components without loss of task success rate identifies removable scaffolding; harness complexity therefore does not need to grow monotonically.
project_ideas.measurement: Marginal task-success contribution and cost delta per harness component per model version; number of components that can be removed with no statistically significant success-rate loss.
project_ideas.name: Harness Ablation Rig
project_ideas.poc: Run the same task suite across two successive model versions with a configurable harness where each component can be toggled; measure success rate, escalation frequency, and cost per task for every harness subset to locate the ablation frontier.
project_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

project_ideas.based_on: Writing 100x more testing code than before
project_ideas.hypothesis: Verification-to-production code ratio scales with machine generation rate rather than human review bandwidth, and pipelines below a threshold ratio exhibit rising defect escape rates that are not detected by human diff review.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between verification-to-production ratio and defect escape rate per generation-volume bucket; ratio threshold at which escape rate stops improving.
project_ideas.name: Verification Ratio Meter
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a repo or pipeline to track verification lines, production lines, generation volume, and post-merge defect escapes per time window; plot escape rate against verification-to-production ratio and detect the knee where escapes fall off.
project_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

project_ideas.based_on: Loop engineering involves setting up systems that prompt Claude in automated loops
project_ideas.hypothesis: Recurring agent loops can run unattended only when explicit idempotency keys, triage-item deduplication, per-loop cost ceilings, and a defined escalation path are enforced, and loops missing these properties fail at a predictable task-ambiguity threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Unattended run success rate, duplicate-action rate, cost per loop run, and the task-ambiguity level at which human escalation becomes mandatory.
project_ideas.name: Loop Ops Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a scheduled loop runner (cadence trigger plus tag-triggered triage) for a morning-check style job over events and PRs, with toggleable idempotency, dedup, cost ceiling, and escalation controls; escalate task scope and ambiguity until autonomy collapses.
project_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

project_ideas.based_on: Calling MCPs and reading inboxes via artifacts
project_ideas.hypothesis: Model-generated interactive artifacts that invoke MCPs and read data sources leak capability unless permissions are granted per artifact instance, and per-instance capability grants reduce unauthorized tool-call surface without reducing task completion rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of tool calls outside the granted scope, task completion rate, and observability coverage of tool-call provenance per artifact instance.
project_ideas.name: Generated Artifact Capability Sandbox
project_ideas.poc: Wrap generated artifacts in a sandbox where each instance receives an explicit scoped capability manifest for its MCP calls and data reads; compare unauthorized-call incidence and task completion against an unscoped baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

project_ideas.based_on: failure accelerates downward spirals
project_ideas.hypothesis: A sustained increase in the rate of minor error-prone actions predicts task failure earlier and with fewer false positives than a threshold on task success rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, and mean time-to-intervention on labeled runs that spiral versus recover.
project_ideas.name: SpiralWatch
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a suite of agent trajectories with injected avoidable small errors; compare a derivative-based drift detector against an end-threshold detector.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

project_ideas.based_on: Betrayal is placed at the bottom of Dante's hell because it undermines trust, the foundation of community.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a multi-agent collaborative task, one compromised agent corrupting shared state causes no downstream task failure when shared state is append-only and attested, but causes measurable task failure with mutable shared state.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate and number of valid downstream states across 100 runs per condition.
project_ideas.name: LedgerAgent
project_ideas.poc: Build two multi-agent task environments (mutable shared state vs append-only attested ledger); inject one agent that writes forged operation results; compare outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

project_ideas.based_on: Upward aim transforms daily actions by aligning them with a transcendent moral framework.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents whose action selection is checked by a constitution layer will achieve higher cumulative success on a long-horizon task than reward-only agents, despite identical step-level rewards.
project_ideas.measurement: Cumulative success rate over 500 episodes and the amount of short-term reward sacrificed per episode.
project_ideas.name: ConstitutionGuard
project_ideas.poc: Implement a task where local reward is noisy and step-optimal choices conflict with terminal goals; compare an LLM action proposer with and without a constitution-checking filter.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

project_ideas.based_on: Write down past misdeeds and mistakes in detail
project_ideas.hypothesis: Policy updates that include structured self-attribution of the model's own actions in failed episodes reduce repeated same-category failures more than updates using only external outcome labels.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of same-category failure across held-out evaluation episodes.
project_ideas.name: Confession Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Build an agent benchmark with recurring decision traps; log full traces and, for failures, generate self-critique before fine-tuning; compare against standard supervised learning on successful traces.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

project_ideas.based_on: Humans remain critical ingredients at local maxima to jump to the next hill.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An autonomous coding loop can produce a reliable plateau signal (stagnating PR acceptance, declining self-improvement, or output churn) that triggers a human retargeting event and materially improves outcomes compared with step-by-step human review or random interventions.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of merged PRs, goal attainment per run, cost per merged PR, and precision/recall of the plateau signal against human-labeled plateaus and intervention outcomes.
project_ideas.name: LoopPlateau
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a bug-fix-to-PR agent loop on a set of synthetic and sample repositories; run three policies: no human until plateau signal, human approval at every step, and random human intervention. At plateau, give the human only a retargeting prompt.
project_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

project_ideas.based_on: Company building is becoming a series of creating loops
project_ideas.hypothesis: A minimal loop abstraction with run, measure, plateau, human-retarget, and compose primitives can express both an engineering coding workflow and a growth testing workflow with less bespoke code and clearer fault boundaries than a conventional agent/DAG framework.
project_ideas.measurement: Lines of code required to express each workflow, time to change an objective, number of human interventions per completed task, and parity of output quality with hand-written orchestration.
project_ideas.name: LoopKit
project_ideas.poc: Build LoopKit and implement two parallel workflows: a coding loop (bug-fix to PR to human review) and a growth variant-generation-and-testing loop, each with local optimizer and human bridge.
project_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

project_ideas.based_on: People want to spend time rather than save time
project_ideas.hypothesis: A consumer AI loop optimized for user-reported enjoyment and felt progress will produce higher voluntary return and retention than an equivalent loop optimized for task speed or output quality.
project_ideas.measurement: D7 voluntary return rate, session count, self-reported mood shift, perceived progress, and correlation between task efficiency and retention.
project_ideas.name: DesireLoop
project_ideas.poc: Build a small consumer 'make me happier' loop (e.g., creative generator with reflection) in two variants: one framed around efficiency and task completion, one framed around emotional progress and fun. Run a two-armed study with volunteer users for two weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

project_ideas.based_on: Frontier models are irrationally priced for certain use cases
project_ideas.hypothesis: For at least three recurring loop archetypes (code modification, growth copy testing, and support drafting), a router that selects between frontier and open-weight models based on per-loop quality bands will reduce inference cost by at least 40% while staying within 5% of frontier-model acceptance quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Inference cost per task, task quality pass rate, router agreement with best available model, and end-to-end loop ROI.
project_ideas.name: LoopModelRouter
project_ideas.poc: Run 200 task instances per archetype on frontier and candidate open-weight models, collect proxy quality labels, train a deterministic router on task features, and simulate routing versus all-frontier within end-to-end loop execution.
project_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

project_ideas.based_on: When frontier models saturate high-profile suites like ARC-AGI-3, a static evaluation harness becomes a lagging indicator
project_ideas.hypothesis: A benchmark pipeline that synthesizes new items from a current model's errors will keep the next-version accuracy below 85% on 1,000 generated items, while accuracy on the original frozen ARC-AGI-3-style suite exceeds 98%.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy on frozen vs. generated benchmark across model checkpoints; time from model release to saturation.
project_ideas.name: AutoEval Churn Engine
project_ideas.poc: Build an LLM-driven mutator that takes failed tasks from an ARC-style grid benchmark, creates semantically constrained variants, filters them with an automatic difficulty judge, then evaluates the next small model on a 1,000-item generated set.
project_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

project_ideas.based_on: Computer-use assistance integrated into a frontier model from the ground up is architecturally different from bolting tool use onto a text model
project_ideas.hypothesis: Intercepting a native CUA model's low-level computer actions and enforcing a reversible-actions-only policy plus user confirmation for high-impact actions will prevent at least 90% of destructive actions while reducing task success by no more than 15% on a 100-task office automation benchmark.
project_ideas.measurement: Policy violations per task, task success rate, human approvals triggered.
project_ideas.name: Action Policy Interceptor for Native CUA
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a CUA-enabled frontier model in a sandboxed VM with a proxy that classifies each action (click, type, file write, network) and allows or blocks it; run the same 100 tasks with and without the interceptor.
project_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

project_ideas.based_on: A 30-million-line formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem is evidence that AI-generated mathematical output can move from informal prose to machine-checkable code artifacts
project_ideas.hypothesis: A 10k-line AI-generated formal proof built in a pinned and reproducible environment will show 20% fewer checker failures than the same proof with floating proof-library dependencies, because the extra failures are dependency-induced, not logical.
project_ideas.measurement: Proof-check pass rate and failure category counts across locked vs. floating builds.
project_ideas.name: Proof Reproducibility Checker
project_ideas.poc: Partition an existing machine-generated formal proof into modules with pinned package locks; rebuild under locked and floating dependency sets and run the proof checker on each.
project_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

project_ideas.based_on: the agent consumes the repository at scale and generates a specification, pre-compiled code, and PRs before human review of only the final 20%
project_ideas.hypothesis: A review strategy that checks an AI-authored repository-scale change against a generated specification and acceptance tests will catch at least 2x more injected semantic defects per reviewer-hour than a full line-by-line diff review of the same PR.
project_ideas.measurement: Semantic defects discovered per reviewer-hour; false-positive review flags.
project_ideas.name: Spec-Only Review Trial
project_ideas.poc: Create a synthetic codebase and an AI PR implementing a feature with dozens of seeded defects; run two groups of engineers, one reading the full diff and one reviewing spec plus acceptance tests plus the final diff; measure defects found.
project_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

project_ideas.based_on: Abstraction should be reframed as context compression
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed token budget, abstractions with higher compression ratios (fewer tokens to represent equivalent functionality) enable agents to solve more complex tasks than lower-compression abstractions.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, error rate, and tokens-per-functionality as a function of abstraction design.
project_ideas.name: Abstraction Compression Benchmark (ACB)
project_ideas.poc: Build a suite of programming tasks where the same functionality is expressed with different abstraction designs (e.g., monolithic vs. layered APIs), run an agent on each under a fixed context window, measure task success.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Compilers will be architected for dialog with AI agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: A compiler that exposes a structured, queryable interface (e.g., requesting specific patterns, negotiating refactors) improves agent repair success and reduces token consumption compared to raw diagnostic text.
project_ideas.measurement: Agent task success rate, number of iterations, token usage.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Dialog Compiler Prototype (ADCP)
project_ideas.poc: Build a wrapper around an existing compiler that provides a conversational API (e.g., ask for errors in JSON, request code patterns across versions), integrate with an agent coding loop, compare against baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

project_ideas.based_on: review or verify code built on AI-defined abstractions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Provenance and explainability artifacts (e.g., abstraction contracts, intent specs) allow human reviewers to validate AI-defined abstractions with higher accuracy and lower cognitive load than reading generated code directly.
project_ideas.measurement: Bug detection rate, time to review, confidence.
project_ideas.name: AI-Abstraction Review Harness (AARH)
project_ideas.poc: Create a system where AI generates code and also produces an abstraction contract and provenance; human reviewers are asked to spot injected bugs under two conditions: with artifacts vs. without.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

project_ideas.based_on: revival of specification languages providing concise intent
project_ideas.hypothesis: Intent-level specifications can regenerate large codebases more reliably (higher fidelity, fewer regressions) than iterating directly on code with AI.
project_ideas.measurement: Regeneration fidelity, test pass rate, human edit effort.
project_ideas.name: Specification-Driven Regeneration Fidelity Check (SDRFC)
project_ideas.poc: Take a codebase, create a concise spec (e.g., Spec++-like), use AI to regenerate code from spec, compare against iterative code editing on metrics like compilation success, test pass rate, edit distance.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

project_ideas.based_on: engineering-to-PM ratio is trending down to 2:1 or even 1:1
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an explicit versioned product-spec and user-feedback capture layer between product intent and AI code generation reduces the ask-to-validated-feature cycle time more than simply swapping prompt templates or model versions.
project_ideas.measurement: Median time from user request to accepted feature; fraction of rework caused by spec drift; number of iterations to meet acceptance criteria.
project_ideas.name: SpecCycle harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small application where user requests enter a spec queue; an AI drafts acceptance criteria and code from the spec; user feedback updates the spec; measure repeated build-validate loops.
project_ideas.video_title: Prompting Is Dead in 6 Months. Andrew Ng, Stanford

project_ideas.based_on: Every time you build something with AI, you take on technical debt
project_ideas.hypothesis: AI-generated PRs that are merged without automated tests, documentation, and an ownership tag become 2x more likely to require defect-fixing changes within 90 days than generated PRs that pass those gates.
project_ideas.measurement: Change frequency, defect density, refactoring cost, and time-to-repair for compliant vs. non-compliant AI-generated modules.
project_ideas.name: DebtGate
project_ideas.poc: Build a pre-merge bot for a repository using AI code generation that flags PRs where generated code lacks test coverage, doc signatures, or assigned maintainer; tag such PRs as unreviewed debt.
project_ideas.video_title: Prompting Is Dead in 6 Months. Andrew Ng, Stanford

project_ideas.based_on: persistent demographic biases
project_ideas.hypothesis: A fixed prompt sweep across demographic descriptors and contexts will surface stereotype patterns that standard safety-filter evaluation misses, making it a reliable regression signal for model releases.
project_ideas.measurement: Stereotype-score distribution, disproportionality across groups, and number of unsafe-by-bias cases that pass a safety-filter-only gate.
project_ideas.name: BiasSweep regression suite
project_ideas.poc: Create a small test harness that samples generated images across a grid of demographic and contextual prompts; score outputs for stereotype proportionality and demographic consistency; run it in CI.
project_ideas.video_title: Prompting Is Dead in 6 Months. Andrew Ng, Stanford

project_ideas.based_on: Wiki pages can have scopes that users can control deterministically
project_ideas.hypothesis: Query-time scope filtering on a shared context store leaks scoped content into lower-privilege contexts at a measurable nonzero rate via summarization and embedding retrieval, while index-time partitioning does not, and the gap is large enough to be a release blocker rather than a rounding error.
project_ideas.measurement: Leakage rate (recovered protected facts per 100 queries) per filter placement and per probe type, plus the false-exclusion rate showing how much legitimate context index-time partitioning costs.
project_ideas.name: Scope-Leak Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a synthetic company wiki with tiered-scope pages, two retrieval modes (index-time partition vs. query-time filter), and three leak probes: top-k direct retrieval, summarization over mixed-privilege results, and nearest-neighbor reconstruction from embedding indexes; run each probe as a low-privilege caller and attempt to recover protected facts.
project_ideas.video_title: Your company brain will leak secrets: how we stopped it for big banks — Tanmai Gopal, PromptQL

project_ideas.based_on: Inject user credentials at the HTTP/SQL layer dynamically based on the initiating user's identity
